weeks.title: How the Web Works: Clients, Servers and HTTP
weeks.summary: Is week aap client-server model, URL ke hisse, DNS se lekar HTTP request tak ka poora safar, HTTP request/response ka structure, status code classes aur latency/bandwidth se page load time ka estimate lagana seekhoge.
concepts: **Client-server model**: browser (user agent) ek **client** hai jo request bhejta hai, aur **server** us request ko process karke response deta hai. Server kabhi khud se baat shuru nahi karta; har exchange client ki request se shuru hota hai. Ek web app mein browser, app server, database sab alag roles hain, par HTTP ke level par baat sirf request aur response ki hoti hai.

**URL anatomy**: `https://shop.example.com:8443/items/list?page=2#reviews` mein scheme `https`, host `shop.example.com`, port `8443`, path `/items/list`, query `page=2` aur fragment `reviews` hai. Port na likho to default lagta hai: `http` ke liye 80, `https` ke liye 443. **Fragment** (`#` ke baad wala hissa) browser ke andar hi rehta hai, server ko request mein nahi jaata.

**DNS se HTTP tak**: browser pehle **DNS** se hostname ka IP address nikaalta hai (OS aur browser cache, phir resolver; har record ka TTL hota hai). Phir server se **TCP connection** banta hai (handshake = 1 RTT), HTTPS ho to uske upar **TLS handshake** hota hai, aur tab jaakar HTTP request jaati hai. Har step mein round trips lagte hain, isliye latency badhti hai.

**HTTP request ka structure**: pehli line request line hai, jaise `GET /items/list?page=2 HTTP/1.1`, jisme method, target aur version hai. Uske baad headers (`Host`, `User-Agent`, `Accept`, `Cookie`), phir ek khaali line, phir optional body. HTTP/1.1 mein `Host` header zaroori hai, kyunki ek IP par kai websites chal sakti hain.

**HTTP response ka structure**: status line jaise `HTTP/1.1 200 OK`, phir headers (`Content-Type: text/html; charset=utf-8`, `Content-Length`, `Set-Cookie`, `Location`), khaali line, aur body. `Content-Type` batata hai body ko kaise samjhein (HTML, JSON, image), isliye galat content type se browser page galat dikhata hai.

**Status code classes**: 1xx informational, 2xx success (200 OK, 201 Created, 204 No Content), 3xx redirection (301 permanent, 302 temporary, 304 Not Modified), 4xx client error (400 Bad Request, 401 Unauthorized, 403 Forbidden, 404 Not Found, 405 Method Not Allowed) aur 5xx server error (500 Internal Server Error, 502 Bad Gateway, 503 Service Unavailable). Pehla digit hi batata hai galti kiski hai.

**Latency vs bandwidth**: latency ek message ke aane-jaane ka time hai (RTT = round-trip time), bandwidth ek second mein kitne bits bhej sakte ho. Rough estimate: total time ≈ (RTTs ki ginti × RTT) + (size in bits ÷ bandwidth). Dhyaan do: network speed **Mbps** (megabits) mein hoti hai aur file size **MB** (megabytes) mein, 1 byte = 8 bits.

**Statelessness**: HTTP stateless hai, yaani server ek request ko pichhli request se apne aap nahi jodta. Login jaisi cheezein yaad rakhne ke liye cookies aur sessions use hote hain (week 7). HTTP/1.1 **persistent connection** (keep-alive) ek TCP connection par kai requests bhejne deta hai, aur HTTP/2 ek connection par kai requests saath-saath (multiplexing) chala sakta hai.

example.problem: Ek student ka laptop 40 Mbps link par hai aur server tak RTT 100 ms hai. 5 MB ka page download karna hai. Maan lo data aane se pehle 2 RTT lagte hain (TCP handshake + request), TLS aur server processing ignore karo. 1 MB = 10⁶ bytes, 1 Mbps = 10⁶ bits/s. Total time kitna hoga?
steps: Latency wala hissa: 2 RTT × 100 ms = 200 ms = 0.2 s.
Size ko bits mein badlo: 5 MB = 5 × 10⁶ × 8 = 40 × 10⁶ bits.
Transmission time = 40 × 10⁶ bits ÷ 40 × 10⁶ bits/s = 1.0 s.
Dono jodo: 0.2 s + 1.0 s = 1.2 s.
Sochne wali baat: chhote pages (jaise 50 KB) ke liye latency hissa zyada bhari padta hai, bade downloads ke liye bandwidth hissa.
Answer: lagbhag **1.2 s**.

mistakes: MB aur Mbps ko same maan lena. 5 MB ko 40 Mbps se seedha divide karke 0.125 s nikaalna galat hai; pehle bytes ko 8 se multiply karke bits banao.
Ye sochna ki URL ka `#section` server tak jaata hai aur server usse alag content bhejega. Fragment sirf browser use karta hai (page ke andar scroll ya client-side routing ke liye).
Har error ko 404 bol dena. Route maujood hai par method galat hai to 405, login nahi hai to 401, permission nahi hai to 403, aur server ke code mein exception aaye to 500.
revision: URL = scheme://host:port/path?query#fragment; fragment server ko nahi jaata.
Order: DNS → TCP handshake → TLS handshake → HTTP request.
Request = request line + headers + blank line + body; HTTP/1.1 mein `Host` zaroori.
2xx success, 3xx redirect, 4xx client ki galti, 5xx server ki galti.
Time ≈ RTTs × RTT + (bytes × 8) ÷ bandwidth.
HTTP stateless hai; state cookies/sessions se aati hai.

questions.question: Browser yeh URL kholta hai: `https://shop.example.com:8443/items/list?page=2&sort=price#reviews`. URL ka kaunsa hissa HTTP request ke saath server tak **nahi** jaata?
questions.explanation: Fragment (`#` ke baad wala hissa) sirf browser ke liye hai, jaise page ke andar kisi section par scroll karna; browser use request mein shaamil nahi karta. Path aur query request line mein jaate hain (`GET /items/list?page=2&sort=price HTTP/1.1`), aur host `Host` header mein, isliye options A, C aur D galat hain. Trap: option A, kyunki log sochte hain query bhi sirf browser ka hissa hai, jabki server isi se filter/sort karta hai.

questions.question: Ek app mein `/login` route sirf GET aur POST accept karta hai. Client `DELETE /login` request bhejta hai. Sabse sahi status code kaunsa hai?
questions.explanation: Resource (`/login`) maujood hai, bas yeh method uske liye allowed nahi hai; iske liye 405 hai, aur response ke `Allow` header mein allowed methods (GET, POST) bataye jaate hain. Option A ka trap: resource mil gaya hai, isliye 404 galat hai. Option D (501) tab hota hai jab server us method ko kisi bhi resource ke liye pehchaanta hi nahi. Option B (403) permission ki kami ke liye hai, method ke liye nahi.

questions.question: 2 MB ki file 16 Mbps link par download karni hai, RTT 80 ms hai. Data aane se pehle 2 RTT lagte hain (TCP handshake + request); TLS aur server time ignore karo. 1 MB = 10⁶ bytes, 1 Mbps = 10⁶ bits/s. Total time kitna hoga?
questions.explanation: Latency: 2 × 80 ms = 0.16 s. Transmission: 2 MB = 16 × 10⁶ bits, aur 16 × 10⁶ ÷ 16 × 10⁶ = 1.0 s. Total = 0.16 + 1.0 = 1.16 s. Option A ka trap: bytes ko bits mein nahi badla (2 ÷ 16 = 0.125 s, plus 0.16). Option B latency bhool jaata hai, aur option C sirf 1 RTT ginta hai.

questions.question: Browser `GET /old-page` bhejta hai aur server jawab deta hai `301 Moved Permanently` ke saath header `Location: /new-page`. Iske baad kya hota hai?
options: Browser apne aap `/new-page` ke liye ek nayi GET request bhejta hai, aur address bar mein `/new-page` dikhta hai
Server andar hi andar `/new-page` ka content nikaal kar usi 301 response ki body mein bhej deta hai
Browser user ko ek error page dikhata hai, kyunki 3xx codes failure hote hain
Browser thodi der baad wapas `/old-page` ko hi dobara request karta hai
questions.explanation: 3xx redirect ka matlab hai 'resource kahin aur hai': browser `Location` header padh kar wahan **nayi request** bhejta hai, isliye do request-response cycles hote hain aur URL badal jaata hai. Option B ka trap: yeh server-side forward/include jaisa hai, redirect nahi; redirect mein kaam client karta hai. Option C galat hai kyunki 3xx error class nahi hai, aur option D `Retry-After`/503 jaisi soch hai.

questions.question: Ek fresh browser (koi cache nahi) mein user `https://www.example.org/` kholta hai. Connection HTTP/1.1 ya HTTP/2 over TCP hai. Sahi order kaunsa hai?
options: TCP handshake → DNS lookup → TLS handshake → HTTP request
DNS lookup → TCP handshake → TLS handshake → HTTP request
DNS lookup → TLS handshake → TCP handshake → HTTP request
HTTP request → DNS lookup → TCP handshake → TLS handshake
questions.explanation: TCP connection ke liye IP address chahiye, isliye DNS sabse pehle. TLS, TCP connection ke upar chalta hai, isliye TLS handshake TCP ke baad. Encrypted channel ban jaane ke baad hi HTTP request jaati hai. Option C ka trap: TLS ko 'security pehle' soch kar TCP se pehle rakhna; par TLS ko bytes bhejne ke liye pehle TCP connection chahiye. Option A mein bina IP ke TCP shuru ho raha hai, jo possible nahi.

questions.question: Plain HTTP/1.1 (TLS nahi), DNS pehle se cached, RTT 50 ms. Browser ek HTML page laata hai jo 5 aur files (3 CSS/JS + 2 images, same server) refer karta hai. Abhi koi TCP connection khula nahi hai; browser ek **persistent** TCP connection kholta hai aur files ek ke baad ek maangta hai (pipelining nahi). Transmission aur server time ignore karo. Saari 6 files aane mein kam se kam kitna time lagega?
questions.explanation: TCP handshake = 1 RTT. Phir HTML ki request-response = 1 RTT, aur baaki 5 files ek ke baad ek = 5 RTT. Total 7 RTT × 50 ms = 350 ms. Option A ka trap: yeh non-persistent connection ka hisaab hai, jahan har file ke liye naya handshake lagta hai (6 × 2 × 50 = 600 ms). Option D handshake bhool jaata hai (6 × 50), aur option B maan leta hai ki saari files ek saath aa gayi.

questions.question: Browser `http://api.example.com/v1/items` kholta hai. URL mein port nahi likha. TCP connection kis port par banega?
questions.explanation: Port na likho to scheme ka default port lagta hai, aur `http` ka default 80 hai. Option A ka trap: 443 `https` ka default hai, `http` ka nahi. Option C (8080) development mein common hai par default nahi, aur option D (21) FTP ka port hai, HTTP ka nahi.

questions.question: Server ne request ka kaam successfully kar diya, par response mein bhejne ke liye koi body nahi hai. Sabse sahi status code kaunsa hai?
options: 200 OK (khaali body ke saath bhi yahi sabse sahi)
questions.explanation: 2xx success hai, aur "success, par body nahi" ka matlab hi 204 No Content hai. Option B (201) tab hai jab naya resource bana ho. Option C ka trap: 304 mein bhi body nahi hoti, par woh 3xx hai aur cache validation ke liye hai ("tumhari cached copy abhi bhi theek hai"). Option D chal to jaata hai, par jab body hai hi nahi to 204 zyada saaf batata hai.

questions.question: Raw HTTP request mein headers khatam hokar body kahan se shuru hoti hai, yeh kaise pata chalta hai?
options: Headers ke baad ek `;` character aata hai
`Content-Length` header ke turant baad body shuru hoti hai
Request line ke end mein likha `BODY:` word batata hai
Headers ke baad ek khaali line aati hai, uske baad body
questions.explanation: Request ka structure hai: request line, headers, ek khaali line, phir optional body. Woh khaali line hi headers ka end batati hai. Option B ka trap: `Content-Length` body ki size batata hai, body kahan se shuru hoti hai yeh nahi; woh bhi bas ek header hai. Options A aur C mein koi aisa marker HTTP mein hota hi nahi.

questions.question: Ek hi IP address (203.0.113.7) par do websites `alpha.test` aur `beta.test` chal rahi hain. Browser `http://beta.test/about` ke liye request bhejta hai. Server kaise decide karta hai ki `beta.test` ka page bhejna hai?
options: IP address se, kyunki browser ne usi IP se connect kiya
`Host` header se, jo HTTP/1.1 mein har request mein zaroori hai
`User-Agent` header se, jisme site ka naam hota hai
questions.explanation: Dono sites ka IP same hai, isliye IP ya TCP connection se farak pata nahi chalta. Browser request mein `Host: beta.test` header bhejta hai, aur isi wajah se HTTP/1.1 mein `Host` zaroori hai. Option A ka trap: ek IP par kai sites ho sakti hain, yahi to problem hai. Option B: path mein hostname hota hi nahi (`GET /about HTTP/1.1`). Option D: `User-Agent` browser ki pehchaan hai, site ki nahi.

questions.question: 50 KB ka page download karna hai, aur data aane se pehle 2 RTT lagte hain. Link X: 100 Mbps, RTT 200 ms. Link Y: 10 Mbps, RTT 20 ms. (1 KB = 10³ bytes, 1 Mbps = 10⁶ bits/s; baaki sab ignore karo.) Kis link par page jaldi aayega?
options: Link Y: lagbhag 80 ms, jabki X par lagbhag 404 ms
Link X: lagbhag 4 ms, jabki Y par lagbhag 40 ms
Link Y: lagbhag 45 ms, jabki X par lagbhag 400 ms
Link Y: lagbhag 40 ms, jabki X par lagbhag 400 ms
questions.explanation: 50 KB = 50 × 10³ × 8 = 400,000 bits. X: 2 × 200 = 400 ms latency + 400,000 ÷ 10⁸ = 4 ms, total 404 ms. Y: 2 × 20 = 40 ms + 400,000 ÷ 10⁷ = 40 ms, total 80 ms. Chhote page par latency haavi padti hai, isliye kam bandwidth wala Y jeetta hai. Option B ka trap: latency bhool kar sirf transmission ginna. Option C bytes ko bits mein nahi badalta (8 se multiply nahi kiya), aur option D sirf latency ginta hai, transmission bhool jaata hai.

questions.question: Fresh browser `https://docs.example.net/` kholta hai. DNS lookup mein 30 ms lagte hain, server tak RTT 40 ms hai. TCP handshake 1 RTT, TLS handshake 1 RTT, aur har HTTP request-response 1 RTT leta hai. HTML ke baad usi **persistent** connection par 2 images ek ke baad ek maangi jaati hain. Transmission aur server time ignore karo. Teeno files aane mein kitna time lagega?
questions.explanation: DNS = 30 ms. Phir TCP (1 RTT) + TLS (1 RTT) + HTML (1 RTT) + 2 images (2 RTT) = 5 RTT × 40 = 200 ms. Total = 30 + 200 = 230 ms. Option D ka trap: DNS ka time bhool jaana. Option A TLS handshake chhod deta hai (30 + 4 × 40). Option C har image ke liye naya connection (TCP + TLS + request = 3 RTT) maan leta hai: 30 + 3 × 40 + 2 × 120 = 390 ms, jo persistent connection mein nahi hota.

questions.question: User address bar mein `http://shop.test/sale` type karta hai. Server ke jawab: `GET http://shop.test/sale` → `301`, `Location: https://shop.test/sale`; `GET https://shop.test/sale` → `302`, `Location: /sale/today`; `GET /sale/today` → `200`. Browser kul kitni HTTP requests bhejega, aur aakhir mein address bar mein kya dikhega?
options: 1 request; server redirects khud follow karke seedha 200 bhej deta hai
questions.explanation: Har 3xx par browser `Location` padh kar ek **nayi** request bhejta hai: pehli request (301), doosri HTTPS wali (302), teesri `/sale/today` (200) = 3 requests. Relative `Location: /sale/today` current URL `https://shop.test/sale` ke against resolve hota hai, isliye final URL `https://shop.test/sale/today` hai. Option C ka trap: relative path ko original `http` URL se jodna. Option A ka trap: sochna ki server redirect khud follow karta hai; redirect client follow karta hai. Option B doosre redirect (302) ko gin hi nahi raha.

questions.question: Plain HTTP/1.1, DNS cached, RTT 60 ms. Browser ek naye persistent connection par HTML laata hai (1 RTT handshake + 1 RTT request). HTML mein 4 images hain. HTML aate hi browser ek **doosra** persistent connection kholta hai (1 RTT handshake), aur images 2 + 2 baant kar har connection par ek ke baad ek maangta hai. Transmission aur server time ignore karo. Saari images kitne time mein aa jaayengi (shuru se)?
questions.explanation: HTML 2 RTT = 120 ms par aata hai. Connection 1 turant 2 images maangta hai: 120 + 60 + 60 = 240 ms. Connection 2 ko pehle handshake chahiye: 120 + 60 = 180 ms, phir 2 images: 180 + 120 = 300 ms. Kaam dono ke khatam hone par poora hota hai, to max(240, 300) = 300 ms. Option A ka trap: doosre connection ka handshake bhool jaana. Option B saari 4 images ek hi connection par maanta hai (120 + 4 × 60), aur option D maanta hai ki saari images ek hi RTT mein saath aa jaayengi.

questions.question: 5 MB file, 20 Mbps link, RTT 100 ms, aur data se pehle 2 RTT lagte hain (1 MB = 10⁶ bytes, 1 Mbps = 10⁶ bits/s). Do upgrades mein se ek hi mil sakta hai: (a) bandwidth 40 Mbps, ya (b) RTT 50 ms. Kaunsa upgrade time zyada ghatayega?
options: RTT wala upgrade: naya time 1.2 s, jabki bandwidth wale se 2.1 s
Bandwidth wala upgrade: naya time 1.2 s, jabki RTT wale se 2.1 s
Bandwidth wala upgrade: naya time 0.325 s, jabki RTT wale se 0.35 s
Dono barabar: dono se time aadha hokar 1.1 s ho jaata hai
questions.explanation: 5 MB = 40 × 10⁶ bits. Abhi: 2 × 0.1 + 40/20 = 0.2 + 2.0 = 2.2 s. (a) 0.2 + 40/40 = 1.2 s. (b) 2 × 0.05 + 2.0 = 2.1 s. Badi file mein transmission haavi hai, isliye bandwidth wala upgrade 1 s bachata hai, RTT wala sirf 0.1 s. Option A ka trap: dono naye times sahi hain par unhe ulte upgrades se jod diya. Option C bytes ko bits mein nahi badalta (5/40 aur 5/20 karta hai). Option D maanta hai ki koi bhi factor-2 sudhaar poora total aadha kar deta hai.

weeks.title: Building Pages with HTML and CSS
weeks.summary: Is week aap HTML document ka structure, semantic tags, block vs inline elements, forms kaise data bhejte hain, CSS selectors aur specificity, box model aur media queries se responsive layout seekhoge.
concepts: **Document structure**: `<!DOCTYPE html>` browser ko standards mode mein rakhta hai. `<html lang="en">` ke andar `<head>` (title, meta charset, viewport, stylesheet links) aur `<body>` (dikhne wala content) hote hain. HTML structure aur meaning batata hai, CSS presentation, aur JavaScript behaviour; is separation se har layer alag se badal sakte ho.

**Semantic tags**: `<header>`, `<nav>`, `<main>`, `<article>`, `<section>`, `<aside>`, `<footer>` content ka role batate hain. Screen readers, search engines aur doosre developers in roles ko samajhte hain; har jagah `<div>` likhne se yeh jaankari kho jaati hai. Headings `<h1>` se `<h6>` tak ek outline banate hain, levels skip mat karo.

**Block vs inline**: block elements (`
`, `

`, `

`, `
`, `
    `) nayi line se shuru hote hain aur poori available width lete hain. Inline elements (``, ``, ``, ``) text ke flow mein rehte hain; unpar `width`/`height` aur vertical margin ka layout par asar nahi hota. `display` property se yeh behaviour badal sakte ho (`inline-block`, `flex`, `grid`).

**Forms**: `<form action="/search" method="get">` batata hai data kahan aur kaise jaayega. Sirf woh controls submit hote hain jinka `name` attribute hai; data `name=value` pairs mein jaata hai. GET mein yeh pairs URL ki query string mein lagte hain, POST mein request body mein. `<label for="email">` ko `<input id="email">` se jodo, taaki label par click aur screen reader dono sahi kaam karein.

**Selectors aur cascade**: type selector `p`, class `.card`, id `#menu`, attribute `[type="email"]`, descendant `nav a`, child `ul > li`, pseudo-class `a:hover`. Jab do rules ek hi property set karein, browser pehle **specificity** dekhta hai aur barabar ho to jo rule baad mein aata hai woh jeetta hai. Inline `style` attribute aur `!important` in sabse upar hain, isliye unhe kam se kam use karo.

**Specificity ginna**: ise (ids, classes/attributes/pseudo-classes, elements) jaisa tuple samjho. `#menu a` = (1, 0, 1), `.link.active` = (0, 2, 0), `nav a.active` = (0, 1, 2). Comparison left se hota hai, isliye ek id kitni bhi classes se bhaari hai. Specificity jeetne ke liye selectors lambe karte jaana maintenance ki problem banta hai; flat class-based CSS behtar hai.

**Box model**: har element content + padding + border + margin hai. Default `box-sizing: content-box` mein `width` sirf content ki hai, padding aur border upar se judte hain. `box-sizing: border-box` mein `width` mein padding aur border shaamil hote hain, isliye layout ka hisaab aasaan hota hai. Do block siblings ke beech vertical margins **collapse** hote hain: gap dono mein se bade margin jitna hota hai.

**Responsive basics**: `<meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1">` ke bina mobile browser page ko desktop width par render karke chhota kar deta hai. **Media queries** jaise `@media (max-width: 600px) { ... }` screen width ke hisaab se rules lagati hain (`max-width` mein boundary value shaamil hai). Fixed px ki jagah `%`, `rem`, `fr` aur flexbox/grid use karo.

example.problem: `.box { width: 200px; padding: 10px; border: 2px solid; margin: 5px; }` hai. Default `content-box` mein box ka visible (border se border) width aur margin samet total horizontal jagah kitni hogi? Aur `box-sizing: border-box` lagane par content ki width kitni bachegi?
steps: Content-box mein `width` sirf content hai: 200px.
Padding dono taraf: 2 × 10 = 20px. Border dono taraf: 2 × 2 = 4px.
Visible width = 200 + 20 + 4 = 224px.
Margin dono taraf jodo: 224 + 2 × 5 = 234px total horizontal jagah.
Border-box mein 200px mein hi padding aur border shaamil hain, to content = 200 − 20 − 4 = 176px, aur visible width 200px hi rehti hai.
Answer: content-box mein **224px visible, 234px total**; border-box mein **content 176px**.

mistakes: Form input mein `id` dena par `name` bhool jaana. Server ko woh field milegi hi nahi, kyunki submission `name` se banta hai, `id` se nahi.
Specificity ko source order se confuse karna. 'Neeche wala rule jeetta hai' sirf tab sach hai jab specificity barabar ho; ek `#id` wala rule upar likha ho tab bhi class wale rules se jeetega.
`width: 100%` ke saath padding lagana aur horizontal scrollbar aa jaana. Content-box mein padding width ke upar judti hai; `box-sizing: border-box` lagao.
revision: Sirf `name` wale form controls submit hote hain; GET = query string, POST = body.
Specificity (ids, classes, elements) pehle, source order sirf tie par.
Content-box: visible width = width + 2·padding + 2·border.
Vertical margins collapse: gap = bada margin.
`max-width: 600px` mein 600px bhi shaamil hai; baad wala matching rule tie par jeetta hai.
Semantic tags + label/for = accessibility ki neev.

questions.question: Email input ke liye kaunsa markup sabse accessible hai, jahan label par click karne se input focus ho aur screen reader field ka naam padhe?
options: `<label>Email</label> <input type="email" name="email">` (label input ke bahar, bina `for`)
questions.explanation: Label ka `for` input ke `id` se match hota hai, isliye label programmatically us input se juda hai: click se focus hota hai aur screen reader field ko 'Email' bolta hai. Option A ka trap: placeholder type karte hi gayab ho jaata hai aur label ki jagah nahi leta. Option C mein `<label>` hai par na `for` hai na input uske andar, isliye jod nahi banta; option B ka `<span>` bas text hai.

questions.question: Is CSS mein `box-sizing` kahin set nahi hai (default). Card ka visible width (border ke ek kinare se doosre tak) kitna hoga?
questions.explanation: Default `content-box` mein `width` sirf content ki hai: 300 + 2 × 20 (padding) + 2 × 5 (border) = 350px. Option A ka trap: `border-box` jaisa sochna, jahan 300px mein sab shaamil hota. Option B border bhool jaata hai, aur option D margin bhi jod deta hai, jabki margin border ke bahar ki khaali jagah hai, visible box ka hissa nahi.

questions.question: User kuch badle bina Go dabata hai. Browser kaunsa URL request karega?
questions.code:
<form action="/search" method="get">
    <input name="q" value="flask">
    <input id="lang" value="en">
    <select name="sort">
        <option value="new" selected>Newest</option>
        <option value="top">Top</option>
    </select>
    <button type="submit">Go</button>
</form>
questions.explanation: Sirf `name` wale controls submit hote hain: `q=flask` aur select ka `sort`. Select ki value chune hue option ka `value` attribute (`new`) hai, dikhne wala text (`Newest`) nahi. Option B ka trap: `lang` input ke paas sirf `id` hai, `name` nahi, isliye woh nahi jaata. Option C display text bhejta hai, aur option D POST ka behaviour hai, jabki yahan method GET hai.

questions.question:
HTML hai `
Home
` aur CSS neeche diya hai. "Home" link ka color kya hoga?
options: browser default link color, kyunki rules aapas mein conflict karte hain
questions.explanation: Specificity: `#menu a` = (1, 0, 1), `nav a.active` = (0, 1, 2), `.link.active` = (0, 2, 0). Comparison left se hota hai aur sirf pehle rule mein id hai, isliye red jeetta hai. Option A ka trap: 'sabse neeche wala rule jeetta hai' ya 'do classes zyada hain'; source order sirf barabar specificity par kaam aata hai. Option D galat hai kyunki conflict ko cascade hamesha resolve karta hai.

questions.question: Viewport width pehle 768px hai, phir 400px. Dono cases mein `.col` ki width kya hogi?
questions.explanation: `max-width: 768px` ka matlab width ≤ 768px, to 768px par pehli query lagti hai aur width 100% hoti hai. 400px par dono queries match karti hain; specificity barabar hai, isliye baad wala rule (90%) jeetta hai. Option A ka trap: `max-width` ko 'strictly less than' samajhna. Option B ka trap: sochna ki pehli matching media query ke baad baaki ignore ho jaati hain; CSS mein saare matching rules cascade mein jaate hain.

questions.question: Do `<div>` normal block flow mein ek ke neeche ek hain (parent ek simple block hai, flex/grid nahi), aur unke beech koi padding, border ya content nahi hai. "One" ke border aur "Two" ke border ke beech vertical gap kitna hoga?
questions.code:
One
Two
.a { margin-bottom: 30px; } .b { margin-top: 20px; }
questions.explanation: Normal flow mein adjacent block siblings ke vertical margins **collapse** hote hain: gap dono margins mein se bade wala hota hai, yaani max(30, 20) = 30px. Option A ka trap: margins ko horizontal ki tarah jod dena (30 + 20). Yeh collapse sirf vertical margins par aur block flow mein hota hai; flex ya grid items ke margins collapse nahi hote, wahan 50px hota. Option D ka 10px difference hai, jiska koi rule nahi.

questions.question: Site ke header mein main navigation links (Home, Courses, Contact) ka group hai. Inhe wrap karne ke liye sabse sahi semantic tag kaunsa hai?
questions.explanation: `<nav>` ka role hi "navigation links ka block" hai, aur screen readers ise landmark ki tarah pehchaan kar seedha wahan jaane dete hain. Option A ka trap: class ka naam `nav` rakhne se meaning browser tak nahi pahunchta, `<div>` generic hi rehta hai. Option B (`<section>`) content ke thematic hisse ke liye hai, aur option D (`<aside>`) side ki related jaankari ke liye.

questions.question: In mein se kaunsa element default roop se **inline** hai?
questions.explanation:
`` inline hai: text ke flow mein rehta hai aur nayi line shuru nahi karta. `

`, `

` aur `
    ` teeno block elements hain jo nayi line se shuru hokar poori width lete hain. Option B ka trap: paragraph text rakhta hai isliye "text jaisa" lagta hai, par khud block hai.

questions.question: `<form action="/signup" method="post">` submit hota hai. Form ka data server tak kaise jaata hai?
options: URL ki query string mein, jaise `/signup?email=...`
Har input ke `id` ke naam se alag headers mein
Request body mein, `name=value` pairs ki tarah
questions.explanation: POST mein form data request **body** mein `name=value` pairs ki tarah jaata hai. Option A ka trap: yeh GET ka behaviour hai, jahan pairs query string mein lagte hain. Option C galat hai kyunki submission `name` se banta hai, `id` se nahi, aur data headers mein nahi jaata. Option B: form cookies nahi banata.

questions.question: In chaar selectors mein se kiski specificity sabse zyada hai?
questions.explanation: Tuples (ids, classes/pseudo-classes, elements): `div ul li a` = (0, 0, 4), `#sidebar .item` = (1, 1, 0), `.nav .item.active` = (0, 3, 0), `ul li a:hover` = (0, 1, 3). Comparison left se hota hai, aur sirf B mein id hai, isliye woh sabse bhaari hai. Option C ka trap: teen classes "zyada" lagti hain, par ek id kitni bhi classes se bhaari hai. Option A ka trap: zyada lamba selector zyada specific nahi hota, elements sabse halke hain.

questions.question: CSS hai `span.tag { width: 200px; height: 50px; }`, aur `display` kahin set nahi hai. Page par `New` kaisa dikhega?
options: Width aur height ka layout par asar nahi; span apne text "New" jitna hi rahega
Span 200px chauda aur 50px ooncha box ban jaayega, text ke flow mein hi
Span nayi line se shuru hokar 200px chauda aur 50px ooncha block banega
Sirf height lagegi; width ignore hogi aur span text jitna chauda rahega
questions.explanation: `<span>` default inline hai, aur inline elements par `width`/`height` ka layout par asar nahi hota; woh apne content jitne hi rehte hain. Box chahiye to `display: inline-block` (ya `block`) lagao. Option B ka trap: yeh `inline-block` ka behaviour hai. Option C span ko block maan leta hai, aur option D aadha rule lagata hai, jabki dono properties ignore hoti hain.

questions.question: `.a` aur `.b` dono `.wrap` ke andar block children hain. Dono ki visible width (border se border) kya hogi, aur `.b` ke content ki width kitni bachegi?
questions.explanation: 40% of 600px = 240px. `.a` (content-box): 240 + 2 × 10 + 2 × 2 = 264px visible. `.b` (border-box): visible 240px hi, aur content = 240 − 20 − 4 = 216px. Option C ka trap: padding aur border sirf ek taraf se ghatana (240 − 10 − 2 = 228). Option A `.a` par bhi border-box laga deta hai, aur option B `.b` ka `box-sizing` ignore kar deta hai.

questions.question: "Buy" link ka final color kya hoga?
questions.code:
Buy
.card .btn { color: red; } div a.primary { color: green; } .btn.primary { color: blue; } a { color: black; }
questions.explanation: Specificity: `.card .btn` = (0, 2, 0), `div a.primary` = (0, 1, 2), `.btn.primary` = (0, 2, 0), `a` = (0, 0, 1). Sabse upar (0, 2, 0) par do rules barabar hain, to source order decide karta hai: baad wala `.btn.primary` jeetta hai, yaani blue. Option A ka trap: barabar specificity mein pehle wale rule ko jitaana. Option B ka trap: (0, 1, 2) mein "zyada selectors" dekhna, jabki middle value 1 hi hai jo 2 se kam hai. Option D sabse kam specific hai.

questions.question: Viewport width 500px, 600px aur 1200px par `.card` ka font-size kya hoga?
questions.explanation: 500px par koi query match nahi karti: 14px. 600px par `min-width: 600px` match karti hai (boundary shaamil hai): 16px. 1200px par dono queries match karti hain; specificity barabar hai, isliye source mein **baad** wala rule (600px wali query, 16px) jeetta hai. Option C ka trap: sochna ki bada breakpoint apne aap jeetta hai; yahan 1000px wali query pehle likhi hai, isliye haar jaati hai. Option A `min-width` ki boundary ko exclude karta hai, aur option D 500px par bhi query laga deta hai.

questions.question: User kuch badle bina Apply dabata hai. Browser kaunsa URL request karega?
questions.code:
<form action="/filter" method="get">
    <input name="q" value="lamp">
    <input type="checkbox" name="color" value="red" checked>
    <input type="checkbox" name="color" value="blue">
    <input type="checkbox" name="color" value="green" checked>
    <input id="page" value="2">
    <button type="submit">Apply</button>
</form>
questions.explanation: GET mein `name=value` pairs query string mein jaate hain. `q=lamp` jaata hai. Checkbox sirf tab submit hota hai jab checked ho, aur ek hi `name` ke kai checked boxes alag-alag pairs bante hain: `color=red&color=green`. Last input ka `name` nahi hai, sirf `id` hai, isliye woh submit nahi hota. Option B ka trap: sochna ki same naam ki aakhri value hi bachti hai. Option C unchecked box ko bhi bhej deta hai, aur option D `id` ko `name` samajh leta hai.

weeks.title: Views with Jinja2 Templates
weeks.summary: Is week aap MVC mein View layer ka role, Jinja2 ka syntax (variables, filters, loops, conditions), autoescaping, template inheritance aur macros, aur templates likhte waqt accessibility ke basic rules seekhoge.
concepts: **View ka role**: MVC mein Model data rakhta hai, Controller request handle karta hai, aur **View** sirf data ko HTML (ya JSON) mein dikhata hai. Flask mein controller `render_template('courses.html', courses=rows, user=u)` call karta hai; template engine context ke variables ko HTML mein bharta hai. View mein database query ya business decision nahi hone chahiye, sirf presentation logic.

**Jinja2 delimiters**: `{{ expr }}` value print karta hai, `{% stmt %}` control (for, if, block, extends) ke liye hai, aur `{# comment #}` output mein nahi aata. `{{ user.name }}` pehle attribute dhoondta hai, phir dict key, isliye object aur dict dono ke saath chalta hai. Jo variable ya key maujood nahi, woh error ke bajaye **undefined** ban kar khaali print hota hai (default setting mein).

**Filters**: `|` ke baad lagte hain aur chain ho sakte hain: `{{ name|title }}`, `{{ items|length }}`, `{{ tags|join(', ') }}`, `{{ price|round(2) }}`. `{{ x|default('N/A') }}` sirf tab N/A deta hai jab `x` undefined ho; khaali string ya 0 ke liye bhi chahiye to `default('N/A', true)` likho.

**Loops aur conditions**: `{% for c in courses %}...{% else %}No courses{% endfor %}` mein `else` tab chalta hai jab list khaali ho. Loop ke andar `loop.index` (1 se), `loop.index0` (0 se), `loop.first`, `loop.last`, `loop.length` milte hain. Jinja mein `break`/`continue` default nahi hai; items skip karne ho to `{% for n in nums if n > 0 %}` likho, jisse `loop.index` sirf filtered items ginta hai.

**Autoescaping**: Flask `.html` templates mein autoescape on rakhta hai, yaani `{{ comment }}` mein `<`, `>`, `&`, quotes HTML entities (`<` etc.) ban jaate hain. Isse user ka diya HTML/JS code chal nahi paata (XSS se bachav). `|safe` filter escaping band karta hai, isliye use sirf trusted, khud banaye HTML par lagao, user input par kabhi nahi.

**Template inheritance**: `base.html` mein common layout aur `{% block content %}{% endblock %}` jaise placeholders hote hain. Child template pehli line mein `{% extends "base.html" %}` likhta hai aur sirf blocks override karta hai; `{{ super() }}` parent block ka content bhi le aata hai. Extends ke baad blocks ke bahar likha text render nahi hota.

**Reuse**: `{% include "_navbar.html" %}` ek partial ko daalta hai, aur `{% macro field(name, label) %}...{% endmacro %}` function jaisa reusable snippet banata hai (form fields ke liye bahut kaam ka). Isse ek hi markup das jagah copy-paste nahi karna padta.

**Accessibility in templates**: `<html lang="en">`, har meaningful image par sahi `alt` (decorative image par `alt=""`), har input ke saath `<label>`, headings ka sahi order, links ka text jo bina context ke bhi samajh aaye ('Download report', 'click here' nahi), aur kaafi colour contrast. Base template mein ek baar sahi kar do to saare pages ko milta hai.

example.problem: Controller `render_template('courses.html', courses=['MAD1', 'DBMS', 'Java'], student='asha')` call karta hai. Neeche wala child template kya render karega?
steps: `courses.html` `base.html` ko extend karta hai, isliye poora skeleton base se aata hai aur sirf `title` aur `content` blocks badalte hain.
`title` block: `Courses | ` ke baad `{{ super() }}` parent ka text `Portal` laata hai, to title `Courses | Portal` banta hai.
`student|title` 'asha' ko `Asha` banata hai, to heading `Hello Asha`.
Loop teen baar chalta hai; `loop.index` 1, 2, 3 aur `loop.length` 3 hai.
List khaali nahi hai, isliye `{% else %}` wala `No courses yet` nahi aata.
Answer: title **Courses | Portal**, heading **Hello Asha**, aur items **1/3: MAD1, 2/3: DBMS, 3/3: Java**.

mistakes: User ke comments par `|safe` laga dena taaki 'formatting dikhe'. Isse koi bhi `<script>` daal kar doosre users ke browser mein code chala sakta hai. User input hamesha escaped rehna chahiye.
Template mein database query ya calculation likhna (jaise har row ke liye total nikaalna). Yeh controller/model ka kaam hai; template ko taiyaar data do.
`loop.index` ko 0 se shuru maanna. Jinja mein `loop.index` 1 se aur `loop.index0` 0 se shuru hota hai.
revision: `{{ }}` print, `{% %}` control, `{# #}` comment.
`default('x')` sirf undefined par; falsy ke liye `default('x', true)`.
`loop.index` 1-based; `for ... if ...` filtered items hi ginta hai.
Autoescape on: `<` → `<`; `|safe` sirf trusted HTML par.
`extends` pehli line; child sirf blocks override kare; `super()` parent ka content.
alt, label, lang, heading order: accessibility basics.

questions.question: Context mein `courses = ['MAD1', 'DBMS']` hai. Yeh template (ek hi line) kya render karega?
questions.code: {% for c in courses %}{{ loop.index }}.{{ c }} {% endfor %}
questions.explanation: Jinja mein `loop.index` 1 se shuru hota hai aur har iteration par badhta hai, isliye `1.MAD1 2.DBMS` aata hai. Option B ka trap: Python ke `enumerate` ki tarah 0 se ginna; woh `loop.index0` hota. Option D maanta hai ki index badhta nahi, aur option C mein order ulta hai.

questions.question:
Ek Flask app `comment.html` template mein `

{{ comment }}

` render karti hai, aur user ne comment mein `hi` likha hai. Default settings mein browser mein kya dikhega?
options: Literal text `hi` dikhega, kyunki `<` aur `>` ko `<` aur `>` mein escape kar diya gaya
Template render nahi hoga aur error aayega
`<b>` tags hata diye jaayenge aur sirf plain 'hi' dikhega
questions.explanation: Flask `.html` templates mein autoescape on hota hai, isliye `{{ comment }}` ke special characters HTML entities ban jaate hain aur browser unhe tags ki tarah nahi, text ki tarah dikhata hai. Option A ka trap: yeh tabhi hota jab `|safe` lagaya jaata (aur tab `<script>` bhi chal jaata). Option D 'sanitizing' hai, jo autoescape nahi karta; woh tags hataata nahi, unhe harmless text bana deta hai.

questions.question: Template ek hi hai. Pehli baar `user = {'name': 'Asha'}` (koi `nickname` key nahi) aur doosri baar `user = {'name': 'Asha', 'nickname': ''}` pass hota hai. Dono outputs kya honge?
questions.code: Hi {{ user.nickname|default('Guest') }}!
questions.explanation: Pehli baar `nickname` key hai hi nahi, to `user.nickname` undefined hai aur `default` 'Guest' deta hai. Doosri baar key maujood hai aur value khaali string hai; `default` sirf undefined par kaam karta hai, isliye khaali string hi print hoti hai: `Hi !`. Option A ka trap: `default` ko Python ke `or` jaisa samajhna; aisa chahiye to `default('Guest', true)` likhna padta. Option C galat hai kyunki default setting mein missing key error nahi deti.

questions.question: `base.html` mein `<title>{% block title %}Site{% endblock %}</title>` hai. Neeche wala `profile.html` render karne par title kya hoga, aur kya "Hello" page par dikhega?
options: `<title>Profile - Site</title>`, aur "Hello" bhi page par dikhega
`<title>Site</title>`, kyunki parent ka block override nahi hota
questions.explanation: Child ka `title` block parent ka block replace karta hai, aur `{{ super() }}` parent ka content 'Site' wapas laata hai, to title `Profile - Site` banta hai. Extends wale template mein blocks ke bahar ka text (yahan "Hello") render nahi hota, kyunki output parent ka layout hai. Option A ka trap: child ko normal page samajhna jahan sab kuch print hota hai. Option B `super()` ko ignore karta hai, aur option D block override ka matlab hi ulta samajhta hai.

questions.question: Header mein ek link hai ``; link ke andar koi text nahi, sirf cart ka icon hai. Image ke liye sabse sahi `alt` kya hai?
questions.explanation: Yahan image hi link ka poora content hai, to uska `alt` hi link ka accessible naam banta hai. Isliye alt mein link ka kaam likho: 'View cart'. Option B ka trap: `alt=""` sirf decorative images ke liye hai jinke saath text pehle se ho; yahan isse link bina naam ka ho jaayega aur screen reader sirf 'link' bolega. Option C filename padhwata hai jo users ke liye bekaar hai, aur option D mein `title` reliable replacement nahi hai.

questions.question: Context mein `nums = [3, 4, 7, 8, 10]` hai. Yeh template (ek hi line) kya render karega?
questions.code: {% for n in nums if n % 2 == 0 %}{{ loop.index }}={{ n }};{% endfor %}
questions.explanation: `for ... if ...` sequence ko pehle filter karta hai, aur `loop` variable sirf un items ko ginta hai jo loop mein aaye: 4, 8, 10 ko index 1, 2, 3 milte hain. Option A ka trap: yeh tab hota jab andar `{% if %}` likha hota aur `loop.index` original list ki position ginta (3 ko bhi count karke). Option B `loop.index0` jaisa hai, aur option C condition ulti padhta hai (odd numbers).

questions.question: Jinja2 template mein ek note likhna hai jo developers ke liye ho aur browser ko bheje gaye HTML mein bilkul na aaye. Kaunsa syntax use karoge?
questions.explanation: `{# ... #}` Jinja comment hai, jo render ke waqt hata diya jaata hai aur output mein nahi aata. Option C ka trap: HTML comment template engine ke liye normal text hai, isliye woh page ke source mein pahunch jaata hai aur koi bhi view-source mein padh sakta hai. Option A value print karta hai, aur option B statement ke liye hai (`note` koi valid tag nahi, error aayega).

questions.question: Context mein `tags = ['flask', 'jinja', 'sql']` hai. `{{ tags|join(', ') }}` kya render karega?
questions.explanation: `join` list ke items ko di gayi string (yahan comma aur space) se jodta hai: `flask, jinja, sql`. Option A ka trap: yeh filter ke bina `{{ tags }}` jaisa Python list ka representation hai. Option C separator ka space bhool jaata hai, aur option D bina separator ke `join` jaisa hai.

questions.question: Controller `courses=[]` (khaali list) pass karta hai. List ke andar kya dikhega?
questions.code:
{% for c in courses %}
  • {{ c }}
    • {% else %}
  • No courses
    • {% endfor %}
options: Template error, kyunki loop khaali list par nahi chal sakta
questions.explanation: Jinja ke `for` loop ka `else` block tab chalta hai jab sequence khaali ho (loop ek baar bhi na chale). Isliye "No courses" wala `<li>` aata hai. Option B ka trap: Python ke `for ... else` jaisa sochna, jahan `else` ka matlab alag hai; Jinja mein yeh "khaali list" ke liye hai. Options C aur D: khaali list par loop bas zero baar chalta hai, error ya "None" nahi aata.

questions.question: Context mein `scores = [70, 85, 90]` aur `avg = 81.6666` hai. `{{ scores|length }} {{ avg|round(1) }}` kya render karega?
questions.explanation: `length` items ginta hai: 3. `round(1)` ek decimal tak normal rounding karta hai: 81.6666 → 81.7 (agla digit 6 hai, isliye upar). Option A ka trap: round ko truncate samajhna (bas kaat dena). Option B length ko last index (2) samajh leta hai, aur option D `round(1)` ka argument ignore karke poore number tak round karta hai.

questions.question: Yeh template kya render karega? (macro definition khud kuch output nahi karti.)
questions.code: {% macro badge(text, kind='info') %}{{ text }}{% endmacro %} {{ badge('New') }}{{ badge('Sold', 'warn') }}
options: Error, kyunki pehli call mein `kind` nahi diya
questions.explanation: Macro function ki tarah kaam karta hai aur default argument bhi leta hai. Pehli call mein `kind` nahi diya, to default `info` lagta hai; doosri call mein `warn` diya gaya. Option A ka trap: default value bhool kar `kind` ko khaali maanna. Option B doosri call ka argument ignore karta hai, aur option C sochta hai ki default ke bawajood argument zaroori hai.

questions.question: `page.html` render karne par title aur body mein kya aayega?
questions.explanation:
Teen levels hain: page → layout → base. Page ke `title` mein `super()` layout ka title block laata hai, jo khud `Shop - ` + `super()` (base ka `Site`) hai: `Cart | Shop - Site`. Layout `body` override nahi karta, isliye page ke `body` mein `super()` base ka `

Base

` laata hai, phir `

Cart

`. Option B ka trap: sochna ki `super()` seedha sabse upar ke base tak jaata hai, beech ka layout skip karke. Option C `super()` ko body mein ignore karta hai, aur option D maanta hai ki child ka block override hi nahi hota.

questions.question: Context mein `students = ['Asha', 'Bilal', 'Chen', 'Dev']` hai. Yeh template (ek hi line) kya render karega?
questions.code: {% for s in students if s != 'Bilal' %}{% if loop.first %}[{% endif %}{{ s }}{% if not loop.last %}, {% else %}]{% endif %}{% endfor %}
questions.explanation: `for ... if` pehle list filter karta hai: Asha, Chen, Dev. `loop` variables sirf in filtered items par chalte hain: Asha par `loop.first` true, isliye `[`; Asha aur Chen ke baad `, `; Dev par `loop.last` true, isliye `]`. Result `[Asha, Chen, Dev]`. Option A ka trap: sochna ki `loop.last` original list ke hisaab se hai aur Dev "last" nahi. Option C Bilal ki jagah khaali item maanta hai, aur option D `loop.first` ko kabhi true nahi maanta.

questions.question: Flask `.html` template (autoescape on) ko context milta hai: `bio = 'hi'` (user ka likha), `tags = ['a', 'b']`, aur `ad_html = 'Sale'` (app ka apna trusted HTML). Page ke HTML source (view-source) mein kya aayega?
questions.code: {{ bio }}|{{ tags|join('+') }}|{{ ad_html|safe }}
questions.explanation: Autoescape on hai, to `{{ bio }}` ke `<` aur `>` entities ban jaate hain: `<i>hi</i>`. `join('+')` deta hai `a+b`. `|safe` escaping band karta hai, isliye `Sale` waisa hi jaata hai. Option A ka trap: autoescape ko bhool jaana (yahi XSS ka raasta hota). Option B `|safe` ka asar ignore karta hai, aur option D dono ko ulta kar deta hai.

questions.question: Context mein `a = 0`, `c = ''` aur `d = 'x'` hain; `b` pass hi nahi kiya gaya. Output kya hoga?
questions.code: {{ a|default('N/A') }} {{ b|default('N/A') }} {{ c|default('N/A', true) }} {{ d|default('N/A', true) }}
questions.explanation: Bina `true` ke `default` sirf undefined par lagta hai: `a = 0` defined hai, to `0`; `b` undefined hai, to `N/A`. `true` ke saath `default` falsy values (khaali string, 0) par bhi lagta hai: `c = ''` → `N/A`, par `d = 'x'` truthy hai, to `x`. Option A ka trap: 0 ko bhi "missing" maanna, jabki `a` par `true` nahi laga. Option B `c` ke `true` argument ko ignore karta hai, aur option C `d` ki asli value bhi badal deta hai.

weeks.title: Models: Databases, ER Design and SQLAlchemy
weeks.summary: Is week aap app ke liye database kyun chahiye, ER diagram se tables kaise banti hain (1:N, M:N), SQL aur ORM ka farak, SQLAlchemy models, relationships, sessions/transactions aur N+1 query problem seekhoge.
concepts: **Database kyun**: Python variables process band hote hi gayab ho jaate hain, aur CSV files mein ek saath kai users likhein to data kharab ho sakta hai. Database persistence, concurrent access, **transactions** (ya to poora kaam ho ya kuch nahi), constraints aur fast querying deta hai. MVC mein Model layer isi data aur uske rules ko represent karti hai.

**Relational model**: data tables mein hota hai; har row ek record, har column ek attribute. **Primary key** (PK) har row ko uniquely pehchaanti hai, **foreign key** (FK) doosri table ki PK ko point karti hai. Constraints jaise `NOT NULL`, `UNIQUE`, FK galat data ko database level par hi rok dete hain, chahe app ke code mein bug ho.

**ER thinking**: pehle entities (Student, Course), unke attributes aur relationships ki cardinality socho. **1:N** (ek User ki kai Posts) mein FK 'N' wali table mein jaati hai: `posts.user_id`. **M:N** (Student–Course) seedha do tables mein nahi aata; ek association table (`enrollment(student_id, course_id)`) banti hai jisme dono FKs hain aur aksar dono milkar PK hote hain. **1:1** ke liye FK par `UNIQUE` lagta hai.

**Normalization ka intuition**: ek fact ek hi jagah store karo. Agar har enrollment row mein course ka title bhi likho to title badalne par saari rows update karni padengi (update anomaly). Course title `course` table mein, aur enrollment mein sirf `course_id` rakho.

**SQL vs ORM**: SQL mein aap queries khud likhte ho; **ORM** (Object-Relational Mapper) class ko table, object ko row aur attribute ko column se map karta hai. ORM boilerplate kam karta hai, values ko safely parameterize karta hai aur Python objects deta hai; par queries chhupi rehti hain, isliye performance samajhne ke liye generated SQL dekhna aana chahiye. Complex reports ke liye raw SQL bhi bilkul theek hai.

**SQLAlchemy model**: `class User(db.Model)` mein `id = db.Column(db.Integer, primary_key=True)`, `email = db.Column(db.String(120), unique=True, nullable=False)`. FK `db.ForeignKey('user.id')` **table.column** naam leti hai (class naam nahi); Flask-SQLAlchemy class `User` ki table ka naam default `user` rakhta hai. `db.relationship('Post', backref='author')` koi column nahi banata; yeh Python side par `user.posts` aur `post.author` jaise attributes deta hai jo FK ke through kaam karte hain.

**Session aur transactions**: `db.session.add(obj)` object ko pending karta hai, `db.session.commit()` transaction ko database mein pakka karta hai, aur error par `db.session.rollback()` sab undo karta hai. Commit ke bina kuch save nahi hota; Flask-SQLAlchemy request ke end mein session hata deta hai aur uncommitted kaam discard ho jaata hai.

**Loading strategy aur N+1**: relationship default mein **lazy** hai: `user.posts` pehli baar access karne par alag SELECT chalti hai. 50 users ki list par har user ke posts padhoge to 1 + 50 queries chalengi, jise **N+1 problem** kehte hain. `selectinload`/`joinedload` jaise eager loading options isse 1–2 queries mein kar dete hain.

example.problem: Ek (fictional) coaching portal mein 3 students aur 2 courses hain. Asha MAD1 aur DBMS mein, Bilal sirf MAD1 mein enrolled hai, Chen kisi mein nahi. Schema banao aur har course ke enrolled students gino.
example.code:
class Student(db.Model):
    id = db.Column(db.Integer, primary_key=True)
    name = db.Column(db.String(80), nullable=False)

class Course(db.Model):
    id = db.Column(db.Integer, primary_key=True)
    code = db.Column(db.String(10), unique=True, nullable=False)

class Enrollment(db.Model):
    student_id = db.Column(db.Integer, db.ForeignKey('student.id'), primary_key=True)
    course_id = db.Column(db.Integer, db.ForeignKey('course.id'), primary_key=True)

-- equivalent SQL report
SELECT c.code, COUNT(e.student_id) AS n
FROM course c
LEFT JOIN enrollment e ON e.course_id = c.id
GROUP BY c.id, c.code
ORDER BY c.code;
steps: Student–Course M:N hai, isliye teesri table `enrollment` banti hai jisme `(student_id, course_id)` composite primary key hai; ek student ek course mein do baar enroll nahi ho sakta.
Rows: enrollment = (Asha, MAD1), (Asha, DBMS), (Bilal, MAD1). Chen ki koi row nahi.
Report ke liye `course` se `LEFT JOIN` karo, taaki zero students wala course bhi aaye.
`COUNT(e.student_id)` sirf non-NULL values ginta hai: DBMS → 1, MAD1 → 2.
Answer: **DBMS 1, MAD1 2**.

mistakes: M:N ko ek column mein comma-separated ids (`'3,7,9'`) rakh kar 'solve' karna. Na FK lag sakti hai, na join ho sakta hai, na index; association table banao.
`db.ForeignKey('User.id')` likhna. FK table ka naam leti hai (`'user.id'`), class ka naam `relationship('User')` mein aata hai.
`add()` ke baad `commit()` bhoolna aur sochna data save ho gaya. Bina commit ke request khatam hote hi changes discard ho jaate hain.
revision: 1:N → FK 'many' side par; M:N → association table.
PK unique pehchaan, FK doosri table ki PK ko point karti hai.
`relationship` column nahi banata; FK hi asli link hai.
add → commit; error par rollback.
Lazy relationship par loop = N+1 queries; eager loading se bachao.
LEFT JOIN + COUNT(column) zero wale rows bhi dikhata hai.

questions.question: Ek student kai courses le sakta hai aur ek course mein kai students hote hain. Relational database mein ise store karne ka sahi tareeka kya hai?
options: `course` table mein `student_ids` column jisme comma-separated ids hon
Ek alag association table (jaise `enrollment`) jisme `student_id` aur `course_id` dono foreign keys hon
Student aur Course ko ek hi table mein merge kar dena
questions.explanation: Yeh many-to-many (M:N) relationship hai, aur relational model mein ise ek association table se represent karte hain jisme har row ek (student, course) pair hai. Option A ka trap: ek column sirf ek course rakh sakta hai, to woh 1:N ban jaata hai. Option B mein na foreign key lag sakti hai na join, aur option D data ko baar-baar duplicate karta hai.

questions.question: Blog app mein ek User ki kai Posts ho sakti hain, par har Post ka ek hi author hai. Foreign key kahan honi chahiye?
options: `posts` table mein `user_id` column, jo `users.id` ko point kare
Dono tables mein ek-doosre ki id
questions.explanation: 1:N relationship mein FK 'many' side (posts) par jaati hai: har post apne ek author ki id rakhti hai. Option A ka trap: user ke paas kai posts hain, to ek `post_id` column sabko nahi rakh sakta. Option C duplicate aur inconsistent data banata hai, aur option D (association table) M:N ke liye hai, yahan zaroorat nahi.

questions.question: `users` mein (1, Asha), (2, Bilal), (3, Chen) hain. `posts` mein teen rows hain: do posts `user_id = 1` ki aur ek `user_id = 3` ki. Yeh query kya return karegi?
questions.code:
SELECT u.name, COUNT(p.id) AS n
FROM users u
LEFT JOIN posts p ON p.user_id = u.id
GROUP BY u.id, u.name
ORDER BY u.id;
questions.explanation: LEFT JOIN Bilal ko bhi rakhta hai, uske post columns NULL ke saath. `COUNT(p.id)` sirf non-NULL values ginta hai, to Bilal ka count 0 hai. Option B ka trap: `COUNT(*)` jaisa sochna, jo NULL wali row ko bhi 1 ginta. Option C INNER JOIN ka result hai, aur option D galat hai kyunki COUNT kabhi NULL nahi deta, 0 deta hai.

questions.question: Neeche ke model ke baare mein kaunsa statement sahi hai? (`User` model ki table `user` hai.)
questions.code:
class Post(db.Model):
    id = db.Column(db.Integer, primary_key=True)
    title = db.Column(db.String(100), nullable=False)
    user_id = db.Column(db.Integer, db.ForeignKey('user.id'), nullable=False)
    author = db.relationship('User', backref='posts')
options: `author` database mein ek alag column banata hai jisme user ka naam store hota hai
`db.ForeignKey('user.id')` galat hai; wahan class ka naam `'User.id'` likhna chahiye
Post bina user ke bhi save ho sakti hai, kyunki relationship optional hota hai
Table mein link sirf `user_id` column se hai; `post.author` se User object aur `user.posts` se us user ki posts ki list milti hai
questions.explanation: `relationship` koi column nahi banata; yeh `user_id` FK ke basis par Python attributes deta hai, aur `backref='posts'` User par ulti taraf ka attribute jodta hai. Option A ka trap: relationship ko column samajh lena. Option B galat hai kyunki `ForeignKey` table.column naam leti hai, class ka naam `relationship('User')` mein aata hai. Option C galat hai kyunki `user_id` par `nullable=False` hai.

questions.question: Ek Flask-SQLAlchemy view `u = User(email='a@x.in')` banata hai, `db.session.add(u)` karta hai, aur `commit()` kiye bina response return kar deta hai. Kya hoga?
options: Row request ke end mein apne aap save ho jaayegi
Row save nahi hogi; request ke end mein session hata diya jaata hai aur uncommitted kaam discard ho jaata hai
Row save ho jaayegi par app restart ke baad hi dikhegi
`add()` hi error dega, kyunki commit ke bina add allowed nahi
questions.explanation: `add()` object ko sirf session mein pending karta hai; database mein pakka karna `commit()` ka kaam hai. Flask-SQLAlchemy app context ke end mein session remove karta hai, aur bina commit wala transaction roll back ho jaata hai. Option A ka trap: 'auto-save' maan lena, jo default behaviour nahi hai. Option D galat hai kyunki add ke baad commit karna normal flow hai, add akela error nahi deta.

questions.question: `User.posts` ek relationship hai jo default (lazy) loading use karta hai. Database mein 50 users hain. Is code se kul kitni SELECT queries chalengi?
questions.explanation: Pehli query saare 50 users laati hai. Lazy loading mein har `u.posts` pehli baar access karne par us user ke liye alag SELECT chalti hai, to 50 aur queries: 1 + 50 = 51. Yahi **N+1 problem** hai. Option B ka trap: yeh `selectinload` jaise eager loading ka count hai, default ka nahi. Option A `joinedload` jaisa ek JOIN maan leta hai, aur option C users wali pehli query bhool jaata hai.

questions.question: Relational table mein **primary key** ka main kaam kya hai?
options: Doosri table ki kisi row ko point karna
Table ki rows ko alphabetical order mein rakhna
Column ki values ko encrypt karna
questions.explanation: Primary key har row ki unique pehchaan hai: do rows ki PK kabhi same nahi ho sakti, aur yahi doosri tables ke foreign keys ka target banti hai. Option B ka trap: yeh foreign key ka kaam hai, jo doosri table ki PK ko point karti hai. Option C (order) aur option D (encryption) PK ka kaam nahi hain.

questions.question: Har User ka zyada se zyada ek Profile ho sakta hai, aur har Profile ek hi User ka hai (1:1). Ise sabse sahi tareeke se kaise model karoge?
options: `profile` table mein `user_id` FK, bina kisi aur constraint ke
`profile` table mein `user_id` FK, aur us column par `UNIQUE`
`user` table mein comma-separated profile ids ka column
questions.explanation: 1:1 ke liye FK ke saath `UNIQUE` lagta hai, taaki ek user ki do profiles ban hi na sakein. Option A ka trap: sirf FK se 1:N banta hai, yaani ek user ki kai profiles allowed ho jaati hain. Option B M:N ke liye hai, aur option D na FK le sakta hai na join, isliye relational design mein galat hai.

questions.question: Wallet transfer mein ek account se ₹500 ghatana aur doosre mein jodna hai. Pehla step hone ke baad server crash ho jaata hai. Database ka kaunsa feature ensure karta hai ki aadha kaam save na rahe?
options: Index, jo rows ko jaldi dhoondhne deta hai
Transaction: poora commit ya poora rollback
Foreign key constraint, jo galat references rokta hai
ORM, jo SQL ki jagah Python objects deta hai
questions.explanation: Transaction kai changes ko ek unit banata hai: commit se pehle crash ho to database saare changes undo kar deta hai, aur paise na kahin ghatte na judte. Option C ka trap: FK galat references rokti hai, adhoora kaam nahi. Option A (index) sirf search fast karta hai, aur option D (ORM) bas code likhne ka tareeka hai; atomicity database ke transaction se aati hai.

questions.question: `enrollment(student_id, course_id, course_title)` table mein har enrollment row ke saath course ka title bhi store hai. Is design ki sabse badi problem kya hai?
options: Koi problem nahi; title saath rakhne se join bachta hai, isliye yahi best hai
`(student_id, course_id)` ko composite primary key nahi bana sakte
Kisi course ke students ginna is design mein possible nahi hai
Title badla to kai rows update karni padengi; ek bhi chhooti to data inconsistent
questions.explanation: Course ka title ek fact hai, par yahan woh har enrollment row mein repeat hai. Title badalne par saari matching rows update karni padti hain, aur ek bhi chhoot gayi to ek hi course ke do title dikhenge: yeh update anomaly hai. Sahi design: title `course` table mein, enrollment mein sirf `course_id`. Option A ka trap: join bachana chhota fayda hai, inconsistent data badi keemat. Options B aur C galat hain: composite PK aur `COUNT` dono yahan bhi kaam karte hain.

questions.question: Is Flask-SQLAlchemy code ke baad kya print hoga?
questions.code:
# course.code par UNIQUE constraint hai; table pehle khaali hai
db.session.add(Course(code='MAD1'))
db.session.commit()

try:
    db.session.add(Course(code='MAD1'))
    db.session.add(Course(code='DBMS'))
    db.session.commit()
except IntegrityError:
    db.session.rollback()

print(Course.query.count())
questions.explanation: Pehla commit MAD1 ko save karta hai. Doosre transaction mein duplicate MAD1 aur DBMS dono pending hain; commit par duplicate se `IntegrityError` aata hai aur `rollback()` us **poore** transaction ko undo karta hai, DBMS ko bhi. Isliye sirf pehla MAD1 bachta hai: 1. Option C ka trap: sochna ki DBMS alag se save ho gaya; ek transaction ya to poora hota hai ya kuch nahi. Option A unique constraint ignore karta hai, aur option D maanta hai ki rollback pehle wala commit bhi undo kar deta hai.

questions.question: Yeh query kya return karegi? (har row: code, a, b)
questions.code:
-- courses:     (1, 'MAD1'), (2, 'DBMS'), (3, 'Java')
-- enrollments: ('s1', 1), ('s2', 1), ('s1', 2)   -- (student_id, course_id)

SELECT c.code, COUNT(*) AS a, COUNT(e.student_id) AS b
FROM courses c
LEFT JOIN enrollments e ON e.course_id = c.id
GROUP BY c.id, c.code
ORDER BY c.id;
questions.explanation: LEFT JOIN se Java bhi aata hai, ek row ke saath jisme `e` ke columns NULL hain. `COUNT(*)` rows ginta hai, to Java ka `a` = 1; `COUNT(e.student_id)` sirf non-NULL ginta hai, to `b` = 0. MAD1 ke 2 enrollments aur DBMS ka 1 dono counts mein same hai. Option A ka trap: sochna ki `COUNT(*)` bhi NULL wali row chhod deta hai. Option B INNER JOIN jaisa result hai, aur option D `COUNT(column)` ko bhi NULL ginne wala maan leta hai.

questions.question: `User.posts` ko `selectinload` se eager load kiya gaya, par `Post.comments` default lazy hai. 20 users hain aur har user ki 3 posts. Kul kitni SELECT queries chalengi?
questions.code:
users = User.query.options(selectinload(User.posts)).all()   # 20 users
for u in users:
    for p in u.posts:              # har user ki 3 posts
        print(p.title, len(p.comments))   # Post.comments: default lazy
questions.explanation: 1 query users ke liye, 1 query (selectinload) saari 60 posts ek saath laane ke liye. Phir har post par `p.comments` lazy hai, to 60 alag queries. Total = 1 + 1 + 60 = 62. Option B ka trap: yeh bina selectinload ka count hai (1 + 20 + 60). Option C maan leta hai ki eager loading comments tak bhi pahunch gayi, aur option D comments ki queries ko users ke hisaab se (20) ginta hai, posts ke hisaab se nahi.

questions.question: Library app: Member kai Books borrow karta hai, ek Book samay ke saath kai Members borrow karte hain, aur har borrow ki date store karni hai. Har Book ka ek hi Publisher hai, aur ek Publisher ki kai Books. Sabse sahi design kaunsa hai?
options: 3 tables; `book` mein `member_id` aur `publisher_id` FKs, aur date bhi `book` mein
4 tables; `publisher` mein `book_id` FK, aur `loan(member_id, book_id, borrowed_on)`
5 tables; publisher–book ke liye bhi association table, aur alag `loan` table
questions.explanation: Member–Book M:N hai, aur borrow date relationship ka attribute hai, isliye association table `loan` banti hai jisme dono FKs aur `borrowed_on` hain. Publisher–Book 1:N hai, to FK "many" side par: `book.publisher_id`. Total: member, book, publisher, loan = 4. Option A ka trap: `book.member_id` sirf ek member rakh sakta hai, M:N nahi. Option B FK ko "one" side par daal deta hai, aur option C 1:N ke liye bina zaroorat association table bana deta hai.

questions.question: Teeno steps ke baad `student` table mein kitni rows hain, aur Bilal ka naam kya store hai?
questions.code:
# student table pehle khaali hai
a = Student(name='Asha')
b = Student(name='Bilal')
db.session.add(a)
db.session.add(b)
db.session.commit()          # (1)

b.name = 'Bilal K'
db.session.rollback()        # (2)

c = Student(name='Chen')
db.session.add(c)
db.session.commit()          # (3)
options: 1 row (sirf Chen); rollback ne sab hata diya
questions.explanation: Step (1) Asha aur Bilal ko commit kar deta hai. Phir naam badla, par commit nahi hua; step (2) rollback sirf us uncommitted change ko undo karta hai, to naam `Bilal` hi rehta hai. Step (3) Chen ko commit karta hai. Total 3 rows. Option C ka trap: sochna ki object par value badalte hi database badal jaata hai; commit ke bina kuch pakka nahi hota. Option D maanta hai ki rollback pehle se committed data bhi hata deta hai, aur option A Chen ka commit bhool jaata hai.

weeks.title: Controllers: Routing, Requests and Validation
weeks.summary: Is week aap controller ka kaam, Flask routing aur URL converters, request object se data padhna, redirect aur `url_for`, Post/Redirect/Get pattern, server-side validation aur business logic ko views se alag rakhna seekhoge.
concepts: **Controller ka role**: request aati hai, controller input padhta aur validate karta hai, model/service ko kaam deta hai, aur decide karta hai ki response kya hoga (template, redirect, JSON ya error). Achha controller **thin** hota hai: usme HTTP se judi baatein hon, business rules alag functions mein.

**Routing**: `@app.route('/courses', methods=['GET', 'POST'])` ek URL rule ko view function se jodta hai. `methods` na do to sirf GET allowed hai (HEAD aur OPTIONS Flask khud sambhalta hai). Koi rule match na kare to **404**, rule match ho par method allowed na ho to **405**.

**Variable rules aur converters**: `/user/<int:uid>` mein converter value ko check bhi karta hai aur type bhi badalta hai: `/user/42` par view ko `uid=42` (int) milta hai, jabki `/user/abc` rule se match hi nahi karta aur 404 aata hai. Default converter `string` hai (slash ke bina koi text), `path` slash bhi le leta hai.

**Request object**: `request.method`, `request.args` (query string), `request.form` (form ka body), `request.get_json()` (JSON body), `request.files`, `request.headers`, `request.cookies`. `request.form['x']` key na mile to Flask khud **400 Bad Request** bhejta hai; optional field ke liye `request.form.get('x', '')` likho.

**Responses**: view string ya `render_template(...)` return kare to 200; `return body, 201` jaisa tuple status set karta hai. `redirect(url)` default mein 302 bhejta hai, `abort(404)` turant error response deta hai. **url_for** (`url_for('endpoint', key=value)`) function ke naam se URL banata hai; jo values rule mein nahi, woh query string ban jaati hain, isliye URLs hard-code nahi karne padte.

**Post/Redirect/Get (PRG)**: form ka POST successful ho to HTML render karne ke bajaye redirect karo. Browser phir GET karta hai, aur user refresh kare to sirf GET dobara hota hai, POST nahi; duplicate order/entry nahi banti. `flash('Saved')` agle page par ek baar dikhne wala message deta hai.

**Server-side validation**: browser ka `required` ya JavaScript check bypass ho sakta hai (curl, devtools), isliye har input server par check karo: strip, type, range, length, format, aur uniqueness (database se). Galat input par form ko errors aur user ki di hui values ke saath dobara dikhao, aur status 400 do; galat data ko kabhi model tak mat jaane do.

**MVC separation**: business rule (jaise 'course full ho to enroll mat karo') ek service function `enroll(student, course)` mein rakho jo exception raise kare. Controller us exception ko flash message ya HTTP status mein badalta hai. Isse rule bina HTTP ke unit test ho sakta hai aur API aur HTML dono controllers ise reuse kar sakte hain.

example.problem: Ek enrollment page banao: GET par form dikhe, POST par roll number validate ho, sahi ho to enroll karke course page par redirect, galat ho to error ke saath form dobara. Teen requests trace karo: GET, POST `roll=abc`, POST `roll=21`.
steps: `GET /courses/3/enroll`: converter `3` ko int banata hai, course mil jaata hai, method GET hai, to khaali form 200 ke saath render hota hai.
`GET /courses/x/enroll` hota to int converter match hi nahi karta aur 404 aata; course id 999 jaisi ho jo DB mein nahi, to `abort(404)`.
`POST` with `roll=abc`: `isdigit()` False hai, to flash message aur form dobara, user ki value ke saath, status 400.
`POST` with `roll=21`: validation pass, `services.enroll` business rule chalata hai, phir `redirect` 302 ke saath `/courses/3` par bhejta hai.
Browser `/courses/3` ke liye GET karta hai; ab refresh karne par enrollment dobara submit nahi hota (PRG).
Answer: responses **200 (form), 400 (form + error), 302 → /courses/3**.

mistakes: `@app.route('/login')` likh kar form ko POST karna aur 405 dekh kar confuse hona. POST handle karna ho to `methods=['GET', 'POST']` likho.
Successful POST ke baad seedha `render_template` return karna. Refresh par browser form dobara bhejta hai; PRG use karo.
Sirf HTML `required`/`maxlength` par bharosa karna. Koi bhi bina browser ke request bhej sakta hai; validation server par zaroori hai.
revision: Default method sirf GET; galat method → 405, koi rule nahi → 404.
`<int:id>` match nahi hua to 404, view chalta hi nahi.
`request.args` = query, `request.form` = form body, `request.get_json()` = JSON.
`url_for` ke extra arguments query string ban jaate hain.
POST success → redirect → GET (PRG).
Validation server par; business rules service functions mein.

questions.question: Route `@app.route('/submit')` ke saath define hai (koi `methods` argument nahi). Ek HTML form `POST /submit` bhejta hai. Response ka status kya hoga?
questions.explanation: `methods` na dene par route sirf GET (aur automatic HEAD/OPTIONS) accept karta hai. URL match hota hai par method nahi, isliye 405. Option B ka trap: 'request fail hui to 404' sochna; 404 tab aata jab koi rule hi match na karta. Option A galat hai kyunki route ka hona kaafi nahi, method bhi allowed hona chahiye, aur option D tab hota jab view ke andar exception aata.

questions.question: `<form action="/signup" method="post">` mein `<input name="email">` hai. Flask view mein is field ki value kahan se milegi?
questions.explanation: POST form ka data request body mein form-encoded hota hai, aur Flask use `request.form` mein deta hai. Option B ka trap: `request.args` sirf URL ki query string hai, jo GET form mein bharti hai. Option C JSON body ke liye hai (jaise `fetch` se `application/json` bhejna), aur option D cookies ke liye; normal form submit unme kuch nahi daalta.

questions.question: Route `@app.route('/user/<int:uid>')` hai aur view `def profile(uid):` hai. Requests `GET /user/42` aur `GET /user/abc` par kya hoga?
options: Dono par view chalta hai; doosre case mein `uid` string `'abc'` hai
`/user/42` theek chalta hai; `/user/abc` par view ke andar `int()` fail hota hai aur 500 aata hai
`/user/42` par `uid` integer 42 hai; `/user/abc` route se match hi nahi karta, isliye 404
questions.explanation: `int` converter matching ke waqt hi check karta hai: digits hon to value int bana kar view ko deta hai, warna rule match nahi hota aur koi aur rule na ho to 404. Option C ka trap: sochna ki conversion view ke andar hota hai aur fail hone par crash (500) hoga; view chalta hi nahi. Option B galat hai kyunki converter type badal deta hai, aur option A converter ko ignore karta hai.

questions.question: Order place karne wala POST handler successful hone par `render_template('done.html')` ke bajaye `redirect(url_for('order_status', oid=o.id))` return karta hai. Iska main fayda kya hai?
options: Server ka load kam hota hai, kyunki redirect ka response chhota hota hai
User page refresh kare to browser sirf GET dobara karta hai, form ka POST nahi, isliye duplicate order nahi banta
HTTP mein POST ke response mein HTML bhejna allowed nahi hai
Redirect se form ka data URL mein aa jaata hai, jo debugging ke liye achha hai
questions.explanation: Yeh Post/Redirect/Get pattern hai: redirect ke baad browser ki history mein aakhri request GET hai, to refresh ya back-forward se order dobara POST nahi hota. Option A ka trap: redirect ko optimisation samajhna; asal mein ek extra request lagti hai. Option C galat hai, POST ka response HTML ho sakta hai; bas refresh par dobara submit ka khatra rehta hai. Option D bhi galat hai, form data redirect URL mein nahi jaata.

questions.question: Route `@app.route('/post/<int:post_id>')` ka view function `show_post` hai. Ek request ke andar `url_for('show_post', post_id=7, ref='mail')` kya return karega?
options: Error, kyunki `ref` route mein nahi hai
questions.explanation: `url_for` rule ke variables (`post_id`) ko path mein bharta hai, aur jo extra arguments rule mein nahi hain (`ref`) unhe query string bana deta hai. Option B ka trap: extra argument ko error samajhna; Flask unhe chupchap query mein daal deta hai. Option D saare values ko query mein daalta hai aur option A unhe path mein, dono rule ko ignore karte hain.

questions.question: Ek controller form ko is function se validate karta hai. Code ka output kya hoga?
questions.explanation: Pehle form mein `'  '.strip()` khaali string hai, to `name` error. `'-5'.isdigit()` False hai (minus sign digit nahi), to `age` = 'number'. Doosre form mein `'075'.isdigit()` True hai aur `int('075')` = 75, jo 18–60 se bahar hai, to sirf `age` = 'range'. Option C ka trap: '-5' ko number maan kar range check par pahunchna. Option D leading zero ko invalid samajhta hai, aur option B `strip()` ko ignore karta hai.

questions.question: Request hai `GET /search?q=lamp&page=2`. Flask view mein `page` ki value kaise padhoge?
questions.explanation: Query string ki values `request.args` mein milti hain. Option A ka trap: `request.form` POST form ki body ke liye hai, URL ke liye nahi. Option C JSON body ke liye hai (yahan body hai hi nahi), aur option D cookies ke liye. Dhyaan rahe: value string `'2'` milti hai; int chahiye to convert karo.

questions.question: View `return redirect(url_for('home'))` karta hai, koi `code` argument nahi diya. Response ka status code kya hoga?
questions.explanation: Flask ka `redirect()` default mein 302 (temporary redirect) bhejta hai, `Location` header ke saath. Option B ka trap: 301 permanent redirect hai, jo sirf `code=301` dene par aata hai. Option A tab hota jab page seedha render hota, aur option D ka redirect se lena-dena nahi.

questions.question: Signup form ke input par HTML `required` aur `maxlength="20"` laga hai. Phir bhi server par validation kyun zaroori hai?
options: Browser ke checks curl, devtools ya script se aasaani se bypass ho sakte hain
HTML `required` sirf Chrome mein kaam karta hai
Server validation se page jaldi load hota hai
Flask HTML attributes padh kar khud validate kar leta hai, isliye alag se kuch nahi likhna
questions.explanation: Koi bhi bina browser ke (curl, script) ya devtools se attributes hata kar request bhej sakta hai, isliye server par har input check karna zaroori hai. Option B ka trap: `required` saare modern browsers mein chalta hai, problem bypass ki hai. Option C ka validation se koi lena-dena nahi, aur option D galat hai: Flask HTML attributes ko dekhta tak nahi.

questions.question: Do POST requests aati hain: pehli ki body `name=Asha` (phone nahi), doosri ki body `phone=999` (name nahi). Dono ka status kya hoga?
questions.explanation: `request.form.get('phone', '')` key na mile to default deta hai, isliye pehli request `ok Asha` ke saath 200. Doosri mein `name` missing hai, aur `request.form['name']` key na mile to Flask khud 400 Bad Request bhejta hai. Option B ka trap: missing `phone` ko error maanna, jabki uske liye `.get()` use hua hai. Option A maanta hai ki missing key par bas khaali value milti hai, aur option C dono ko ek jaisa samajhta hai.

questions.question: Do apps mein route alag hai: App 1 mein `@app.route('/files/<fp>')`, App 2 mein `@app.route('/files/<path:fp>')`. Dono ko `GET /files/docs/a.txt` milta hai. Kya hoga?
questions.explanation: Default `string` converter slash ke bina text leta hai, isliye `docs/a.txt` (jisme slash hai) App 1 ke rule se match hi nahi karta: 404. `path` converter slash bhi le leta hai, to App 2 ko poora `docs/a.txt` milta hai. Option D ka trap: sochna ki string converter pehla hissa le kar baaki chhod dega; rule poora URL match karta hai ya bilkul nahi. Option A dono converters ko ek jaisa maanta hai.

questions.question: Order form ka POST handler do versions mein hai. Version P (PRG): success par `redirect(url_for('order', oid=o.id))`. Version R: success par seedha `render_template('done.html')`. Dono mein user ek baar order submit karta hai, phir result page par 2 baar refresh dabata hai (browser poochhe to resubmit confirm karta hai). Har version mein kul kitne orders banenge?
questions.explanation: P mein POST ke baad browser GET `/order/...` karta hai, to refresh sirf woh GET dohraata hai: 1 order. R mein result page khud POST ka response hai, to har refresh wahi POST dobara bhejta hai: 1 + 2 = 3 orders. Isi duplicate se bachne ke liye PRG hai. Option D ka trap: pehle submit ko ginti mein na lena. Option B maanta hai ki refresh kabhi POST nahi dohraata, aur option C PRG ke redirect ko ignore karta hai.

questions.question: Server-side validation ka yeh function teen inputs par chalaya gaya. Output kya hoga?
questions.explanation: Pehla: `' 61 '` strip hokar `'61'`, digits hain, par 61 > 60, to `range`; email theek. Doosra: `'-5'.isdigit()` False hai (minus sign digit nahi), to `roll` aur `range` check chalta hi nahi (`elif`); email mein `@` nahi, to `email`. Teesra: roll missing, default `''` digits nahi, to `roll`. Option A ka trap: -5 ko number maan kar range error dena. Option C missing field ko pass kar deta hai, aur option D 61 ko range ke andar maanta hai (boundary galat padhna).

questions.question: Char requests aati hain: (i) `DELETE /items`, (ii) `GET /items/x7`, (iii) `POST /items/5`, (iv) `HEAD /items/5`. Flask kaunse status codes dega?
questions.explanation: (i) `/items` rule match hota hai par DELETE allowed nahi: 405. (ii) `x7` int nahi, to `<int:iid>` match hi nahi karta: 404. (iii) Rule match hai par `methods` nahi diya, to sirf GET allowed: 405. (iv) GET allowed ho to HEAD Flask khud sambhalta hai: 200 (body ke bina). Option A ka trap: HEAD ko bhi "allowed nahi" maanna. Option B (i) mein method galat ko 404 bolta hai, aur option C converter ki galti ko 400 maanta hai.

questions.question: Business rule ek service function mein hai jo exception raise karta hai (controller baad mein ise flash message ya status mein badlega). Output kya hoga?
questions.explanation: Pehli `bilal` call: list mein nahi, size 1 < 2, to add → True. Doosri `bilal` call: pehle se list mein hai → False (capacity check tak pahunchti hi nahi). `chen`: size ab 2 ≥ cap 2, to `CourseFull` raise hota hai, `'ok'` wali line skip hoti hai aur `except` mein `'full'` judta hai. Students 2 hi rehte hain. Option B ka trap: capacity check bhool jaana. Option A aur D duplicate check ko ignore karte hain (bilal ko do baar add karna).

weeks.title: Designing REST APIs with JSON
weeks.summary: Is week aap API aur web page ka farak, REST ke principles, resources aur URI design, HTTP methods ki safe/idempotent properties, APIs ke liye sahi status codes, JSON aur OpenAPI se API ko document karna seekhoge.
concepts: **API kyun**: HTML page insaan ke liye hai, API program ke liye. Ek hi backend ko browser ka JavaScript, mobile app aur doosri services API se use karti hain, isliye response data (aksar JSON) hota hai, layout nahi. MVC mein API ka 'view' JSON serializer hai.

**REST ke principles**: client-server alag, **stateless** (har request apni poori jaankari, jaise auth token, saath laaye; server pichhli request yaad nahi rakhta), cacheable responses, layered system, aur **uniform interface**: har resource ka URI hai, aur use standard HTTP methods se representations (JSON) bhej kar badla jaata hai.

**Resources aur URIs**: URI mein noun rakho, verb nahi; method hi verb hai. Collection `/api/v1/courses`, ek item `/api/v1/courses/12`, sub-resource `/api/v1/students/17/enrollments`. Filtering, sorting aur pagination query string mein: `?status=open&sort=-created&page=2&limit=20`. `/getCourses` ya `/deleteCourse?id=12` RPC style hai, REST nahi.

**Methods**: GET padhta hai, POST collection mein naya item banata hai, PUT poora resource replace karta hai (ya given URI par banata hai), PATCH kuch fields badalta hai, DELETE hataata hai. **Safe** = server state nahi badalta (GET, HEAD). **Idempotent** = ek baar karo ya das baar, server state par asar same (GET, HEAD, PUT, DELETE). POST na safe hai na idempotent: do baar bhejo to do items ban sakte hain; PATCH bhi guaranteed idempotent nahi (jaise 'stock mein 1 jodo').

**Status codes for APIs**: 200 OK (data ke saath), 201 Created (naya resource, `Location` header mein uska URI), 204 No Content (success, body nahi, jaise DELETE), 400 Bad Request (malformed JSON ya galat type), 401 Unauthorized (authentication nahi hai ya invalid), 403 Forbidden (pehchaan liya par permission nahi), 404 Not Found, 409 Conflict (duplicate ya version clash), 422 (aksar validation errors ke liye). Errors bhi JSON body mein, ek consistent format mein do: `{"error": "..."}`.

**JSON**: text format jiske types hain object, array, string, number, `true`/`false`, `null`. Python mapping: dict → object, list/tuple → array, `True` → `true`, `None` → `null`. Keys hamesha double-quoted strings hote hain. Response par `Content-Type: application/json` hona chahiye; Flask view dict return kare to Flask khud JSON bana deta hai (`jsonify` bhi yahi karta hai).

**Versioning, pagination, OpenAPI**: breaking change ke liye `/api/v2/` jaisa version rakho, taaki purane clients na tootein. Badi lists hamesha paginate karo. **OpenAPI** ek YAML/JSON specification hai jo har path, method, parameters, request/response schemas aur status codes describe karti hai; isse interactive docs, client code aur contract tests generate hote hain.
