document.querySelector('#list').addEventListener('click', (e) => { console.log(e.target.tagName, e.target.closest('li').id); });
questions.explanation: Click button par hua, to `e.target` button hai (`tagName` HTML mein uppercase: `BUTTON`). Event bubble hokar `ul` ke listener tak pahunchta hai, aur `closest('li')` button se upar jaakar pehla `li` dhoondta hai: `item-7`. Yahi event delegation hai. Option A ka trap: `e.target` ko woh element maanna jis par listener laga hai. Option B target ko li maanta hai, aur option D sochta hai ki `closest` sirf element khud ko check karta hai.

questions.question: API se naam aaya: `name = ''`. Code A: `el.innerHTML = name`. Code B: `el.textContent = name`. Dono mein kya hoga?
options: Dono mein yeh poori string sirf text ki tarah dikhegi
Dono mein img banega aur `onerror` wala code chal jaayega
A mein string text ki tarah dikhegi; B mein img banega aur `onerror` chalega
A mein img banega aur `onerror` chal sakta hai; B mein string text dikhegi
questions.explanation: `innerHTML` value ko HTML ki tarah parse karta hai: `` element banta hai, `src=x` load fail hota hai aur `onerror` ka code chalta hai, yaani DOM-based XSS. `textContent` value ko plain text rakhta hai, to `<` `>` sab text ki tarah dikhte hain. Option C ka trap: dono ko ulta yaad rakhna. Option A maanta hai ki browser `innerHTML` ko bhi escape karta hai, aur option B `textContent` ko bhi parse karne wala maanta hai.

questions.question: Is code ka output kis order mein aayega?
questions.explanation: Pehle synchronous code: 1, 6. Phir saare microtasks: pehla `.then` 3 print karta hai aur ek naya timeout (4) queue karta hai; doosra `.then` 5. Phir macrotasks apne queue order mein: pehle wala timeout 2, phir baad mein queue hua 4. Option A ka trap: `setTimeout(..., 0)` ko Promise se pehle chalne wala maanna. Option C maanta hai ki microtask ke andar laga timeout aage nikal jaata hai, aur option D Promise callbacks ko synchronous code ke beech chala deta hai.

questions.question: Network theek hai, aur server `/api/users/9` par status 404 aur body `{"error": "no user"}` bhejta hai. Console mein kya aayega?
options: Sirf `sent`; 404 par Promise kabhi settle nahi hota
questions.explanation: `getUser(9)` turant Promise return karta hai aur `await` sirf us function ko rokta hai, isliye `sent` pehle aata hai. 404 par `fetch` resolve hota hai (reject nahi), par code `res.ok` (false) check karke khud Error throw karta hai, jo `.catch` mein `err HTTP 404` deta hai. Option C ka trap: `res.ok` check na hota to `name undefined` aata; yahan check hai. Option B `await` ko poora program rokne wala maanta hai, aur option D sochta hai ki 404 par Promise latak jaata hai.

questions.question: Har student ko 5 grace marks milte hain; 50 ya usse upar pass hai, aur 90 ya upar walon ke 2 points, baaki pass walon ka 1 point. Code ka output kya hoga?
questions.explanation: `map`: 50, 87, 72, 35, 96. `filter` (≥ 50): 50, 87, 72, 96. `reduce`: 50 → 1, 87 → 1, 72 → 1, 96 → 2, total 5. Option A ka trap: grace marks jodne se pehle filter lagana (82, 67, 91 → 1 + 1 + 2 = 4), jisse 45 + 5 = 50 wala student chhoot jaata hai. Option B 87 ko bhi 90 ke upar maan leta hai, aur option D sirf 1-point wale pass students ginta hai.

questions.question: Is code ka output kis order mein aayega?
questions.explanation: `b()` synchronously `b1` print karta hai aur `a()` call karta hai, jo `a1` print karke `await null` par ruk jaata hai. Ab control wapas top-level par: `c`. Phir microtask mein `a` aage badhta hai: `a2`, aur `a` khatam hone par `b` ka `await` poora hota hai: `b2`. Option A ka trap: `await` ko poora program rokne wala maanna. Option B maanta hai ki async function ka pehla hissa bhi baad mein chalta hai, aur option C `b2` ko `a2` se pehle rakhta hai, jabki `b` ko `a` ke poora hone ka intezaar hai.

weeks.title: Web Application Security Essentials
weeks.summary: Is week aap authentication aur authorization ka farak, passwords ko salt aur slow hashing se store karna, sessions aur tokens, aur teen sabse common attacks (XSS, CSRF, SQL injection) ke defences, saath hi HTTPS kya bachata hai aur kya nahi, seekhoge.
concepts: **Authentication vs authorization**: authentication = 'tum kaun ho?' (login, password, token check); authorization = 'tumhe yeh karne ki ijaazat hai?' (role, ownership check). Authorization **har request par server par** check karo: sirf button chhupa dena kaafi nahi, kyunki koi bhi seedha `/notes/9/delete` hit kar sakta hai (IDOR bug). Har user ko kam se kam zaroori permission do (least privilege).

**Password storage**: password kabhi plain text ya reversible encryption mein mat rakho. Har user ke liye random **salt** lo aur slow password-hashing function (bcrypt, scrypt, Argon2, PBKDF2 with lakhon iterations) se hash karo; salt aur hash dono store karo. Salt ki wajah se same password wale do users ke hash alag hote hain aur precomputed (rainbow) tables bekaar ho jaate hain; slowness brute force ko mehnga banati hai. Flask world mein Werkzeug ke `generate_password_hash`/`check_password_hash` yahi karte hain.

**Sessions aur tokens**: login ke baad server session banata hai aur browser ko cookie deta hai (`HttpOnly`, `Secure`, `SameSite`). Login par session id naya banao (session fixation se bachav), expiry rakho aur logout par session khatam karo. APIs aksar **bearer token** (`Authorization: Bearer ...`) use karti hain; signed tokens (jaise JWT) server par state nahi maangte, par expiry se pehle unhe revoke karna mushkil hota hai.

**XSS (Cross-Site Scripting)**: attacker ka input page mein code ban kar doosre users ke browser mein chalta hai: stored (DB mein save hua comment), reflected (URL parameter seedha page mein) ya DOM-based (`innerHTML`). Defence: output par context ke hisaab se escaping (Jinja autoescape on rakho, `|safe` aur `innerHTML` se bacho), Content-Security-Policy header, aur session cookie par `HttpOnly` taaki script use chura na sake.

**CSRF (Cross-Site Request Forgery)**: browser cookies apne aap har matching request ke saath bhejta hai, chahe request kisi aur site ke page ne trigger ki ho. Attacker ka page ek hidden form aapke `POST /transfer` par auto-submit kar sakta hai, aur logged-in user ki cookie saath chali jaati hai. Defence: har state-changing form mein random **CSRF token** jo server session se match kare (Flask-WTF), `SameSite=Lax/Strict` cookies, `Origin` header check, aur GET se kabhi state mat badlo.

**SQL injection**: user input ko string formatting se SQL mein jodne par input query ka structure badal deta hai. SQL mein `AND` ki precedence `OR` se zyada hai, isliye injected `OR` ka asar hamesha 'saare rows' nahi hota; par khatra har haal mein hai. Defence: **parameterized queries** (`execute('... WHERE name = ?', (name,))`) ya ORM; table/column naam user se lene hon to whitelist; DB user ko minimum privileges.

**HTTPS/TLS**: teen cheezein deta hai: confidentiality (beech mein koi padh nahi sakta), integrity (koi badal nahi sakta) aur server authentication (certificate se pata chalta hai ki sahi server hai). Login form, cookies aur tokens sirf HTTPS par bhejo, aur HSTS header se browser ko hamesha HTTPS use karne ko kaho. HTTPS app ke andar ke bugs (XSS, SQLi, galat authorization) se nahi bachata.

example.problem: Sirf Python standard library se ek secure login check banao: PBKDF2 se salted hash, constant-time comparison aur parameterized query. Teen login attempts ka result kya hoga: sahi password, galat password, aur username mein injection `x' OR '1'='1`?
steps: `hash_password` har user ke liye 16 random bytes ka salt banata hai aur `salt$hash` format mein store karta hai; database leak ho to bhi password seedha nahi dikhta.
`login('asha', 's3cret!')`: row milti hai, stored salt se dobara hash banta hai aur match hota hai → True.
`login('asha', 'guess')`: hash match nahi hota → False. `hmac.compare_digest` comparison ka time input par depend nahi karne deta (timing attack se bachav).
`login("x' OR '1'='1", ...)`: `?` placeholder ki wajah se poori string sirf ek value hai; is naam ka user nahi, `fetchone()` None deta hai → False.
Answer: **True False False**.

mistakes: `md5(password)` ya `sha256(password)` bina salt ke store karna. Yeh fast hash hain; GPU par arbon guesses per second ho jaate hain aur same passwords ke hash same dikhte hain.
Sochna ki form ko POST bana diya to CSRF se bach gaye. Attacker ki site bhi POST form auto-submit kar sakti hai; CSRF token ya SameSite chahiye.
Sirf frontend par admin button chhupa kar authorization 'implement' karna. Server par har endpoint mein role/ownership check karo.
revision: Authentication = kaun ho; authorization = kya kar sakte ho (server par, har request).
Password: per-user salt + slow hash; kabhi plain ya encrypted nahi.
XSS → output escape, `|safe`/`innerHTML` se bacho, CSP, HttpOnly.
CSRF → token + SameSite + Origin check; GET se state mat badlo.
SQLi → parameterized queries; `AND` ki precedence `OR` se zyada.
HTTPS = confidentiality + integrity + server authentication; app bugs nahi rokta.

questions.question: Riya login karke `/admin/reports` kholti hai aur 403 Forbidden milta hai, kyunki uska role 'student' hai. Yeh kis cheez ka check fail hua?
options: Authentication: server ne Riya ko pehchaana hi nahi
Authorization: Riya pehchaani gayi, par is resource ki permission nahi hai
Input validation: request ka data galat tha
questions.explanation: Riya logged in hai, yaani authentication ho chuka; server ne uska role dekh kar access mana kiya, jo authorization hai, aur 403 isi ka status hai. Option A ka trap: dono 'auth' words ko mix karna; pehchaan na hoti to response 401 hota. Options C aur D ka is scenario se lena-dena nahi.

questions.question: Ek naye app mein users ke passwords store karne ka sabse sahi tareeka kya hai?
options: Plain text mein, taaki 'forgot password' par user ko uska password email kar sakein
`sha256(password)` bina salt ke, kyunki SHA-256 secure hash hai
Har user ke liye random salt ke saath slow password-hashing function (bcrypt, scrypt, Argon2 ya PBKDF2), aur salt + hash store karna
Password ko server ki secret key se AES encrypt karke store karna
questions.explanation: Salted slow hash one-way hai, har user ke liye alag hai aur har guess ko mehnga banata hai. Option B ka trap: SHA-256 secure hash hai, par password ke liye bahut fast hai aur bina salt ke same passwords ka same hash aata hai. Option D reversible hai: key leak hui to saare passwords khul jaate hain. Option A sabse kharab hai; reset ke liye password bhejne ki jagah reset link bhejo.

questions.question: Is code ka output kya hoga?
questions.code:
import hashlib

def h(pw, salt):
    return hashlib.pbkdf2_hmac('sha256', pw.encode(), salt, 100_000).hex()

a = h('secret', b'salt-A')
b = h('secret', b'salt-B')
c = h('secret', b'salt-A')
print(a == b, a == c, len(a))
questions.explanation: Same password par alag salt se alag hash aata hai (`a == b` False), aur same password + same salt se hamesha same hash (`a == c` True); isi se login verify hota hai. SHA-256 ka output 32 bytes hai aur `.hex()` har byte ko 2 characters mein likhta hai, to length 64. Option C ka trap: bytes (32) aur hex string ki length (64) ko mix karna. Option A salt ka asar ignore karta hai, aur option B maanta hai ki hashing random hai.

questions.question: Ek banking app ka `/transfer` endpoint session cookie se user pehchaanta hai. In mein se kaunsa measure **akela** CSRF attack ko nahi rokta?
options: Endpoint ko GET se badal kar sirf POST accept karna
Har state-changing form mein random CSRF token jo server session wale token se match ho
Server par `Origin` header check karke sirf apni site se aayi requests maanna
questions.explanation: Attacker ki site par ek hidden `<form method="post">` JavaScript se auto-submit ho sakta hai, aur browser user ki cookie saath bhej deta hai; isliye sirf POST bana dena kaafi nahi (haan, GET se state na badalna phir bhi zaroori hai). Option B ka token attacker ko pata nahi hota, option C cross-site request par cookie bhejna rokta hai, aur option D doosri site ka origin pakad leta hai. Trap: option A ko 'secure method' samajhna.

questions.question: Flask app mein autoescape on hai. Comments page ka kaunsa template line stored XSS ka raasta kholti hai, agar `c.text` user ka likha comment hai?
questions.explanation: `|safe` Jinja ko batata hai ki yeh string trusted HTML hai, isliye escaping band ho jaati hai aur comment mein likha `<script>` sabke browser mein chalta hai. Option A ka trap: plain `{{ }}` dekh kar dar jaana; autoescape on hai to yeh safe hai. Option B (`|e`) explicitly escape karta hai, aur option D sirf ek number print karta hai.

questions.question: `users` table mein teen rows hain: ('asha', '1234'), ('bilal', '0000'), ('chen', '9999'). Ek vulnerable login yeh query banata hai, aur attacker username field mein `x' OR '1'='1` aur pin mein `0000` daalta hai. Query kya return karegi?
questions.code:
u = "x' OR '1'='1"
p = "0000"
q = f"SELECT name FROM users WHERE name = '{u}' AND pin = '{p}'"
rows = conn.execute(q).fetchall()
options: Teeno users (asha, bilal, chen), kyunki `'1'='1'` hamesha true hai
Koi row nahi, kyunki 'x' naam ka user nahi hai
questions.explanation: Banne wali query: `WHERE name = 'x' OR '1'='1' AND pin = '0000'`. `AND` ki precedence `OR` se zyada hai, to yeh `name = 'x' OR ('1'='1' AND pin = '0000')` hai, jo sirf pin 0000 wali row (bilal) par true hai. Option A ka trap: `'1'='1'` dekhte hi 'sab rows' maan lena, precedence bhool kar. Quotes balanced hain, isliye option D bhi galat hai. Fix: parameterized query.

questions.question: Site HTTPS par chal rahi hai. In mein se kya HTTPS **nahi** deta?
options: Confidentiality: beech mein koi data padh nahi sakta
Integrity: raaste mein koi data badal nahi sakta
Server authentication: certificate se sahi server ki pehchaan
App ke XSS ya SQL injection bugs se bachav
questions.explanation: HTTPS/TLS network par data ko encrypt, tamper-proof aur sahi server se juda rakhta hai: A, B, C teeno deta hai. Par app ke andar ke bugs (XSS, SQL injection, galat authorization) encrypted channel ke andar bhi waise hi kaam karte hain. Trap: "HTTPS = secure app" maan lena; HTTPS sirf transport ko secure karta hai.

questions.question: Login form par server email aur password check karke pata lagata hai ki request bhejne wala Kabir hai. Yeh step kya kehlata hai?
questions.explanation: Authentication ka sawaal hai "tum kaun ho?", aur password check karke pehchaan pakki karna wahi hai. Option A ka trap: authorization agla step hai, "Kabir ko yeh karne ki ijaazat hai ya nahi?". Option C data ko chhupana hai, aur option D database design ka concept hai.

questions.question: Search feature user ke input ko SQL query mein use karta hai. SQL injection se bachne ka sabse sahi tareeka kya hai?
options: Input mein se single quotes hata dena hi kaafi hai
Search form ko GET se POST bana dena
Parameterized query (`?` placeholder) ya ORM use karna
questions.explanation: Parameterized query mein value query ke structure se alag jaati hai, isliye input kitna bhi ajeeb ho, woh sirf data rehta hai, SQL nahi banta. Option A ka trap: quotes hatana adhoora hai (numbers, comments, aur encoding ke tareeke bach jaate hain) aur sahi naam jaise O'Brien tod deta hai. Option B aur D ka injection se koi lena-dena nahi: POST body bhi utni hi controllable hai, aur HTTPS sirf transport secure karta hai.

questions.question: Riya aur Sameer dono ka password `sunflower9` hai. App har user ke liye random salt lekar PBKDF2 se hash store karti hai. Salt ka sabse bada fayda kya hai?
options: Dono ke hash alag hote hain, aur precomputed (rainbow) tables bekaar ho jaati hain
Salt hash ko reversible bana deta hai, taaki bhoole password wapas mil sakein
Salt hashing ko fast banata hai, isliye login jaldi hota hai
Salt ko secret rakhna padta hai; leak hua to hash turant toot jaata hai
questions.explanation: Salt har user ke hash ko unique banata hai: same password ke bhi do alag hash, aur attacker ek bani-banayi table se sab passwords nahi pakad sakta; use har user ke liye alag mehnat karni padti hai. Option B galat hai: hash one-way hi rehta hai. Option C ka trap: speed nahi, slowness (iterations) brute force ko mehnga banati hai. Option D: salt hash ke saath store hota hai aur secret nahi hota; uska kaam uniqueness hai.

questions.question: Attacker ki site par ek hidden form hai jo page khulte hi `POST https://bank.test/transfer` auto-submit karta hai. Logged-in victim us site par jaata hai aur uski session cookie request ke saath chali jaati hai. Kaunsa defence is attack ko rokega?
options: Transfer endpoint ko GET ki jagah sirf POST accept karne dena
Har form mein random CSRF token, jo server session se match kare
Saare passwords ko salt ke saath bcrypt se hash karna
Poori bank site ko sirf HTTPS par chalana aur HSTS lagana
questions.explanation: Attacker ki site cookie to bhijwa sakti hai, par victim ke session ka random CSRF token nahi jaanti, isliye server request reject kar deta hai. Option A ka trap: endpoint pehle se POST hai aur attacker ka form bhi POST hi bhej raha hai. Option C password storage ke liye hai, aur option D: HTTPS par bhi browser cookie apne aap bhejta hai.

questions.question: Vulnerable login mein attacker pin field mein `x' OR name = 'chen` daalta hai. Query kaunsi rows return karegi?
questions.code:
# users: ('asha', '1234'), ('bilal', '0000'), ('chen', '9999')
u = "asha"
p = "x' OR name = 'chen"
q = f"SELECT name FROM users WHERE name = '{u}' AND pin = '{p}'"
rows = conn.execute(q).fetchall()
questions.explanation: Final query: `WHERE name = 'asha' AND pin = 'x' OR name = 'chen'`. `AND` ki precedence `OR` se zyada hai, to yeh `(name = 'asha' AND pin = 'x') OR name = 'chen'` hai. Pehla hissa kisi row par true nahi (asha ka pin x nahi), doosra sirf chen par true: result chen. Option B ka trap: har injected `OR` ko "saari rows" maanna. Option C maanta hai ki username sahi hai to woh aa jaayega, aur option A injection ka asar hi ignore karta hai.

questions.question: Login check teen attempts par chalaya gaya. Output kya hoga?
questions.code:
import hashlib, hmac

def make(pw, salt):
    return hashlib.pbkdf2_hmac('sha256', pw.encode(), salt, 1000)

salt = b'k9'
stored = make('Tiger#7', salt)
tries = ['tiger#7', 'Tiger#7', 'Tiger#7 ']
print([hmac.compare_digest(make(t, salt), stored) for t in tries], len(stored))
questions.explanation: Hash exact bytes par chalta hai: `tiger#7` (chhota t) aur `Tiger#7 ` (end mein space) alag inputs hain, isliye sirf beech wala match karta hai: `[False, True, False]`. `pbkdf2_hmac` sha256 ke saath raw **bytes** deta hai, jo 32 bytes hain. Option B ka trap: hex string ki length (64 characters) se confuse hona; yahan `.hex()` nahi laga. Option D case ko ignore karta hai, aur option A space ko bhi. `compare_digest` constant-time comparison karta hai, taaki timing se kuch leak na ho.

questions.question: Teen bugs: (i) comment DB mein save hota hai aur sabke liye `{{ c.text|safe }}` se dikhaya jaata hai; (ii) search page URL ke `q` parameter ko `You searched: {{ q|safe }}` se seedha dikhata hai; (iii) JS `el.innerHTML = location.hash.slice(1)` karta hai. Kis bug mein kaunsa XSS type hai?
questions.explanation: (i) Payload database mein save hota hai aur har dekhne wale ko lagta hai: stored. (ii) Payload request (URL) se aakar usi response mein wapas aata hai: reflected. (iii) Payload server tak gaya hi nahi (fragment server ko nahi jaata), browser ka JS use `innerHTML` mein daalta hai: DOM-based. Option B ka trap: (i) aur (ii) ko ulta karna. Option C (iii) ko reflected maanta hai, jabki yahan server ka koi role nahi, aur option D type ke farak ko ignore karta hai.

questions.question: Ravi logged in hai aur apne session ka sahi CSRF token ke saath `POST /notes/9/delete` bhejta hai. Note 9 Meera ka hai. Kya hoga, aur sahi fix kya hai?
options: 403 milega, kyunki `login_required` ownership bhi check karta hai
Note delete ho jaayega; fix: owner check karke `abort(403)`
404 milega, kyunki `get_or_404` sirf owner ke notes dhoondta hai
Request CSRF ki wajah se fail hogi, isliye koi fix zaroori nahi
questions.explanation: `login_required` sirf authentication check karta hai ("koi logged in hai"), authorization nahi. Note maujood hai, CSRF token valid hai, to code note delete kar dega: yeh IDOR bug hai. Fix: har request par server mein ownership check karke 403 dena. Option A ka trap: login check ko permission check samajhna. Option C maanta hai ki `get_or_404` owner dekhta hai, jabki woh sirf id dhoondta hai. Option D galat hai, kyunki token Ravi ka apna aur sahi hai.

weeks.title: Testing Web Applications
weeks.summary: Is week aap unit, integration aur end-to-end tests ka farak, pytest ke conventions aur fixtures, Flask test client se routes test karna, mocking se external services alag karna, aur line vs branch coverage ka matlab seekhoge.
concepts: **Tests kyun**: har change ke baad poori app haath se check karna possible nahi. Automated tests regression pakadte hain, refactoring ka confidence dete hain aur code ka behaviour document karte hain. CI (jaise har push par tests chalna) ke saath toota hua code main branch tak nahi pahunchta.

**Test pyramid**: neeche bahut saare **unit tests** (ek function/class akele, milliseconds mein), beech mein kam **integration tests** (routes + database + templates saath, jaise test client se), aur upar thode **end-to-end tests** (real browser Playwright/Selenium se poora user flow). Upar jaate hue tests slow, mehnge aur flaky hote hain, par real user ke zyada kareeb.

**pytest basics**: pytest `test_*.py` ya `*_test.py` files mein `test` se shuru hone wale functions apne aap dhoondta hai. Simple `assert` likho; fail hone par pytest dono values dikhata hai. `@pytest.mark.parametrize` ek test ko kai inputs par chalata hai, aur `with pytest.raises(ValueError):` check karta hai ki exception aaya. Har test **Arrange-Act-Assert** pattern mein aur baaki tests se independent ho.

**Fixtures**: `@pytest.fixture` setup code ko reusable banata hai; test parameter mein fixture ka naam likho aur pytest use inject kar deta hai. `yield` se pehle setup, baad mein teardown. Default scope **function** hai, yaani har test ke liye fixture naye sire se banta hai; `scope='module'` ya `'session'` se ek baar banta hai aur share hota hai. Common fixtures `conftest.py` mein rakhte hain.

**Flask test client**: app factory `create_app({'TESTING': True, ...})` se test config (jaise in-memory SQLite) do. `app.test_client()` bina real server aur network ke requests seedha WSGI app ko bhejta hai: `client.get('/')`, `client.post('/login', data={...}, follow_redirects=True)`, `client.post('/api/x', json={...})`. Response par `status_code`, `data`, `get_json()` aur headers check karo.

**Mocking**: payment gateway, email, time ya randomness jaise external/non-deterministic cheezon ko test mein asli nahi chalate. `unittest.mock.patch` unhe ek fake object se badal deta hai jiska return value tum set karte ho, aur baad mein `call_count`/`assert_called_with` se check kar sakte ho ki code ne use sahi call kiya. Patch wahan karo jahan object **lookup** hota hai.

**Coverage**: `coverage run -m pytest` phir `coverage report -m` batata hai kaunsi lines chali. **Line coverage** = kitni executable lines kam se kam ek baar chali; **branch coverage** = har `if` ke True aur False dono raaste chale ya nahi. 100% line coverage ka matlab bug-free nahi: bina assert ke chali line bhi 'covered' hai, aur boundary values (jaise exactly 50) alag se test karne padte hain.

example.problem: Week 6 ke create-course API ke liye do pytest tests likho: create par 201, duplicate par 409. Fixture har test ke liye fresh in-memory database deta hai. Dono tests pass honge?
example.code:
# conftest.py
import pytest
from myapp import create_app, db

@pytest.fixture
def client():
    app = create_app({'TESTING': True, 'SQLALCHEMY_DATABASE_URI': 'sqlite:///:memory:'})
    with app.app_context():
        db.create_all()
        yield app.test_client()
        db.drop_all()

# test_courses.py
def test_create_course(client):
    r = client.post('/api/v1/courses', json={'code': 'MAD1'})
    assert r.status_code == 201
    assert r.get_json()['code'] == 'MAD1'

def test_duplicate_course(client):
    client.post('/api/v1/courses', json={'code': 'MAD1'})
    r = client.post('/api/v1/courses', json={'code': 'MAD1'})
    assert r.status_code == 409
steps: pytest `test_courses.py` ke dono `test_` functions collect karta hai aur `client` parameter dekh kar `conftest.py` ka fixture inject karta hai.
Fixture ka scope function hai: har test se pehle naya app aur khaali database, test ke baad `drop_all()`.
`test_create_course`: khaali DB mein MAD1 banta hai → 201, JSON mein `code` MAD1 → pass.
`test_duplicate_course`: is test ka DB bhi khaali hai, to pehli POST 201, doosri 409 → pass.
Agar fixture `scope='module'` hota to dono tests ek DB share karte, aur doosre test ki pehli POST hi 409 deti; tests order par depend karne lagte. Isliye isolated fixtures behtar hain.
Answer: **dono tests pass** hote hain, bina real server chalaye.

mistakes: Tests ko ek-doosre ke data par depend karwana (ek test user banaye, agla use use kare). Order badalte hi tests toot jaate hain; har test apna data khud banaye.
Test mein asli payment/email API call karna. Tests slow, flaky aur mehnge ho jaate hain; mock karo.
Coverage % ko hi goal bana lena. Bina meaningful `assert` ke 100% coverage bhi bugs nahi pakadta; boundaries aur error paths test karo.
revision: Unit (bahut, fast) → integration (kam) → e2e (thode, slow).
pytest: `test_*.py`/`*_test.py` files, `test*` functions, plain `assert`.
Fixture default scope = function: har test ke liye naya setup.
Test client: bina server ke `client.get/post`, `status_code`, `get_json()`.
`patch` = external cheez ko fake se badlo, lookup wali jagah par.
100% line coverage ≠ 100% branch coverage ≠ bug-free.

questions.question: Ek test headless browser kholta hai, login page par email aur password type karta hai, Submit dabata hai, aur check karta hai ki dashboard par user ka naam dikh raha hai. Yeh kis type ka test hai?
questions.explanation: Real browser se poora user flow (UI → server → database → wapas UI) chalaya ja raha hai, yahi end-to-end test hai. Option C ka trap: integration test bhi kai parts saath chalata hai, par test client wala test browser, HTML rendering aur JavaScript ko nahi chalata. Unit test (option B) ek function ko akela test karta hai, aur option D code chalata hi nahi.

questions.question: Project folder mein bina kisi argument ke `pytest` chalaya gaya (default settings). In mein se kaunsa function test ki tarah collect hoga?
questions.explanation: Default mein pytest sirf `test_*.py` ya `*_test.py` files dekhta hai, aur unke andar `test` se shuru hone wale functions. Option D dono shartein poori karta hai. Option A ka trap: file sahi hai par function ka naam `test` se shuru nahi hota. Option B mein function sahi hai par file `cart.py` pattern se match nahi karti, aur option C mein file sahi par function galat.

questions.question: Abhi tests sirf `grade(95)` aur `grade(70)` check karte hain. 100% line coverage ke liye kaunsa ek call aur jodna hoga?
questions.explanation: 95 'A' wali line aur 70 'P' wali line chala chuke hain; sirf `return 'F'` bachi hai, jo m < 50 par chalti hai, isliye `grade(30)`. Option B ka trap: 50 boundary hai aur test karna achha hai, par `50 >= 50` True hai, to woh bhi 'P' deta hai aur nayi line nahi chalata. Options A aur D 'A' wali line hi dobara chalate hain.

questions.question: Ek test file mein yeh fixture aur chaar tests hain. `pytest -s` chalane par 'setup' kitni baar print hoga?
questions.explanation: Fixture ka default scope function hai, to har us test ke liye alag se setup chalta hai jo use maangta hai: `test_home`, `test_login`, `test_logout` = 3 baar. `test_utils` fixture nahi maangta, isliye uske liye setup nahi. Option A ka trap: fixture ko 'file mein ek baar' samajhna; woh `scope='module'` par hota. Option C maanta hai ki fixture har test ke liye chalta hai, chahe test use maange ya nahi.

questions.question: Dice-roll feature ko deterministic test karne ke liye `random.randint` ko patch kiya gaya. Code ka output kya hoga?
questions.explanation: `roll()` har call par `random.randint` ko module se lookup karta hai, aur `with` block ke andar woh mock hai jo hamesha 4 lautata hai. Mock har call ginta hai: do `roll()` = `call_count` 2. Option B ka trap: sochna ki `return_value` ek hi baar use hota hai ya mock sirf pehli call ginta hai. Option D maanta hai ki patch `roll` ke andar tak nahi pahunchta, jabki lookup call ke waqt hota hai.

questions.question: Is function ka sirf ek test hai: `assert shipping(600, True) == 0`. Coverage ke baare mein kaunsa statement sahi hai?
options: Line aur branch dono coverage 100% hain, kyunki har line chali
Branch coverage 100% hai par line coverage nahi
Line coverage 100% hai, par branch coverage nahi, kyunki dono `if` ka False raasta kabhi nahi chala
Line coverage 100% nahi hai, kyunki `fee = 0` do baar likha hai
questions.explanation: `shipping(600, True)` mein dono conditions True hain, to saari lines chalti hain: line coverage 100%. Par branch coverage dono raaste maangta hai, aur `is_member` False ya `total ≤ 500` wala case kabhi test nahi hua; non-member chhota order (fee 50) bilkul untested hai. Option A ka trap: line coverage ko hi poora coverage samajhna. Option B ulta hai (branches poore hon to lines bhi chal chuki hoti hain), aur option D ka duplicate line se koi lena-dena nahi.

questions.question: Test pyramid ke hisaab se ek healthy project mein sabse zyada sankhya mein kaunse tests hone chahiye?
questions.explanation: Pyramid ke neeche unit tests hain: fast (milliseconds), sasta aur stable, isliye sabse zyada wahi. Option A ka trap: E2E real user ke sabse kareeb hain, par slow, mehnge aur flaky, isliye pyramid ke upar thode se. Option C beech mein kam sankhya mein, aur option D automated tests ka hissa hi nahi.

questions.question: Test mein `client = app.test_client()` ke baad `client.get('/')` chalaya. Andar kya hota hai?
options: Ek real server port par start hota hai aur request network se jaati hai
Ek headless browser khulta hai aur page load karta hai
Request bina real server aur network ke seedha WSGI app ko di jaati hai
Sirf template render hota hai, view function nahi chalta
questions.explanation: Test client request ka `environ` bana kar seedha Flask ke WSGI app ko call karta hai: poora routing, view aur template chalta hai, par koi server ya network nahi. Isliye integration tests fast rehte hain. Option B ka trap: yeh E2E tools (Playwright/Selenium) ka kaam hai. Option A galat hai, aur option D bhi: view function poora chalta hai.

questions.question: `parse_age('abc')` ko `ValueError` raise karna chahiye. pytest mein ise check karne ka sahi tareeka kaunsa hai?
questions.explanation: `pytest.raises` context manager pass hota hai sirf jab block ke andar woh exception aaye, warna test fail. Option B ka trap: function exception raise karta hai, return nahi, to yeh line test ko error ke saath tod degi. Option C mein bhi call pehle hi exception de dega. Option D har case mein pass ho jaata hai, chahe exception aaye ya na aaye, isliye kuch test hi nahi karta.

questions.question: Is file par `pytest` chalaya gaya. Kitne tests collect honge?
questions.explanation: `parametrize` ek test ko 3 inputs par chalata hai, to `test_grade` se 3 tests. Phir `test_grade_type` aur `test_boundary`: 2 aur. `helper_marks` `test` se shuru nahi hota, isliye collect nahi hota. Total 3 + 2 = 5. Option B ka trap: parametrized function ko ek hi test ginna. Option C helper ko bhi test gin leta hai (3 + 2 + 1), aur option A sirf parametrize ke cases ginta hai.

questions.question: Test mein `checkout()` ko asli gateway ke bina chalana hai. Kaunsa patch target `checkout()` ke andar fake `charge` lagayega?
questions.explanation: `from payments import charge` ne `shop` module mein apna naam `charge` bana liya hai, aur `checkout()` isi naam ko `shop` mein lookup karta hai. Isliye patch wahan karo jahan lookup hota hai: `shop.charge`. Option B ka trap: `payments.charge` badalne se `shop` ke paas pehle se rakha purana reference nahi badalta, aur asli gateway call ho jaayega. Option C mein module path hi nahi hai, aur option D `checkout` ko hi fake kar deta hai, to asli code test hi nahi hota.

questions.question: `pytest -s` (dono files) chalaya gaya. Output mein `db` aur `client` kitni-kitni baar print honge?
questions.explanation: `client` default (function) scope ka hai, to har test ke liye naya: 3 + 2 = 5 baar. `db` module scope ka hai: har test module (file) mein ek baar banta hai aur usi file ke tests share karte hain, to 2 files = 2 baar. Option A ka trap: module scope ko session scope (poore run mein ek baar) samajhna. Option B module scope ko ignore karta hai, aur option D `client` ko bhi module scope ka maan leta hai.

questions.question: Sirf yeh do tests hain aur dono pass hote hain. Coverage ke baare mein kaunsa statement sahi hai?
options: Line coverage 100%, par branch coverage sirf 50%
Line aur branch dono 100%; phir bhi (1200, None) wala case test nahi hua
Line coverage 80%, kyunki `d += 5` wali line kabhi nahi chali
Branch coverage 75%: coupon wale `if` ka False raasta nahi chala
questions.explanation: Pehla test dono `if` ke True raaste chalata hai (saari lines), doosra dono ke False raaste. To line aur branch dono 100% hain. Par coverage har branch ko alag se dekhta hai, combinations ko nahi: (1200, None) yaani sirf 5 ka discount kabhi test nahi hua. Option A ka trap: branch coverage ko combinations ginna samajhna. Option C aur D maante hain ki koi line ya False raasta chhoot gaya, jabki doosra test unhe chala deta hai.

questions.question: Time ko deterministic banane ke liye `time.time` patch kiya gaya. Output kya hoga?
questions.code:
from unittest.mock import patch
import time

def stamp(label):
    return f'{label}@{int(time.time())}'

with patch('time.time', return_value=1700000000.9) as t:
    a = stamp('x')
    b = stamp('y')
print(a, b, t.call_count)
questions.explanation: `stamp` har call par `time.time` ko `time` module mein lookup karta hai, aur patch wahi naam badalta hai, isliye dono baar fake value 1700000000.9 milti hai. `int()` decimal kaat deta hai (round nahi karta): 1700000000. Mock do baar call hua, to `call_count` 2. Option A ka trap: `int()` ko rounding samajhna. Option B call count ko ek maanta hai, aur option C sochta hai ki patch `stamp` tak pahunchta hi nahi.

questions.question: Yeh file `pytest` se chalayi gayi (tests file ke order mein chalte hain). Phir sirf `pytest -k again` chalaya gaya. Dono baar results kya honge?
options: Dono runs mein saare tests pass, kyunki har test alag hai
Poore run mein dono fail, aur akele mein bhi fail
`test_add` fail, `test_add_again` pass; akele mein bhi pass
questions.explanation: Module-level `users` list tests ke beech share hoti hai. Poore run mein `test_add` asha jodta hai aur pass hota hai; `test_add_again` mein asha pehle se hai, to `ValueError` aur test fail. `-k again` mein sirf woh test chalta hai, list khaali hai, to pass. Yahi tests ke ek-doosre par depend karne ki problem hai; har test apna data khud banaye (fixture se). Option B ka trap: har test ko automatically fresh state wala maanna. Options C aur D order ka asar ulta padhte hain.

weeks.title: Modern HTML: Browser APIs, Components, PWAs, Accessibility and SEO
weeks.summary: Is week aap HTML5 ke native features aur browser APIs (Web Storage, IndexedDB, Geolocation), Web Components ka idea, PWA ke liye manifest aur service worker, aur accessibility aur SEO ke practical rules seekhoge.
concepts: **Modern HTML**: aaj HTML ek 'living standard' hai jo lagatar update hota hai. Semantic elements ke saath native media (`<video controls>`, `<audio>`), drawing ke liye `<canvas>` aur `<svg>`, aur `<dialog>` jaise interactive elements aa gaye, jinke liye pehle plugins ya bhaari JavaScript lagta tha.

**Native form features**: `type="email"`, `number`, `date`, `url` aur attributes `required`, `min`, `max`, `pattern`, `maxlength` browser mein hi validation aur sahi mobile keyboard dete hain. Yeh UX ke liye hai, security ke liye nahi: devtools, curl ya script inhe bypass kar sakte hain, isliye server-side validation hamesha zaroori hai.

**Storage APIs**: `localStorage` per-origin, browser band karne ke baad bhi rehta hai; `sessionStorage` sirf us tab tak. Dono synchronous hain aur **sirf strings** rakhte hain (number dalo to string ban jaata hai; objects ke liye `JSON.stringify`/`JSON.parse`). Yeh server ko apne aap nahi jaate, cookies jaate hain. Bade ya structured data ke liye async **IndexedDB**. XSS hone par script localStorage padh sakti hai, isliye usme secrets mat rakho.

**Aur browser APIs**: Geolocation (user permission aur secure context zaroori), History API (`pushState` se bina reload URL badalna, single-page apps ke liye), WebSockets (server aur browser ke beech two-way connection, jaise live chat), Notifications. Use se pehle feature detection karo: `if ('geolocation' in navigator) { ... }`.

**Web Components**: framework ke bina reusable elements. **Custom Elements**: `customElements.define('user-card', class extends HTMLElement { ... })`; naam mein hyphen zaroori hai aur letters lowercase hone chahiye, taaki future ke built-in tags se clash na ho. **Shadow DOM** component ke andar ka DOM aur CSS bahar se alag (encapsulated) rakhta hai, aur `<template>`/`<slot>` markup ko reuse karne dete hain.

**PWA (Progressive Web App)**: normal website jo installable aur offline-capable ho. **Web App Manifest** (JSON: name, icons, `start_url`, `display`) install ka data deta hai. **Service worker** ek background script hai jo page aur network ke beech proxy ki tarah `fetch` events pakadta hai aur Cache API se offline responses de sakta hai. Yeh sirf secure context (HTTPS, ya development mein localhost) par chalta hai, aur default **scope** uski script ki directory hoti hai.

**Accessibility (a11y)**: pehle semantic HTML (`<button>`, `<nav>`, `<label>`), ARIA sirf tab jab native element na ho; galat ARIA na hone se bhi bura hai. Har kaam keyboard se ho sake, focus dikhe, images par alt ho, aur normal text ka contrast kam se kam 4.5:1 (WCAG AA). Dynamic updates (jaise 'Saved') ko `aria-live` region se screen reader tak pahunchao.

**SEO basics**: har page ka unique `<title>` aur meta description, ek saaf `<h1>`, crawlable `<a href>` links (sirf JS click handler nahi), server par rendered content, `robots.txt`, `sitemap.xml` aur canonical URL. Fast, mobile-friendly pages rank aur conversion dono mein madad karte hain. Semantic HTML accessibility aur SEO dono ko ek saath fayda deta hai.

example.problem: Ek Flask app ko offline-capable banana hai. Service worker register karo aur static files cache-first strategy se do. Kya chalega offline, aur `sw.js` kahan serve karna chahiye?
steps: Feature detection: purane browser mein `serviceWorker` nahi hai to kuch nahi hota, site normal chalti hai.

`/sw.js` root par hai, to default scope `/` hai aur poori site ke pages control hote hain. Flask mein iske liye ek route chahiye jo file root URL par de (sirf `/static/` mein rakhne se scope `/static/` reh jaata).
`install` event par teen URLs cache mein store hote hain.
Har `fetch` par pehle cache dekha jaata hai (cache-first); mila to wahi, warna network.
Offline hone par `/`, CSS aur JS cache se khulte hain; jo URLs cache mein nahi (jaise API calls) woh fail honge, unhe UI mein sambhaalo.
Files badlo to `CACHE` ka naam (`static-v2`) badlo, warna users purana version dekhte rahenge.
Answer: **cached shell offline khulta hai**, aur `sw.js` ko **site root `/sw.js`** par serve karna chahiye.

mistakes: `<div onclick="...">` ko button bana dena. Woh keyboard se focus nahi hota aur screen reader use button nahi batata; `<button>` use karo.
localStorage se number padh kar seedha jodna (`getItem('n') + 1`). Value string hai, to concatenation hota hai; `Number(...)` ya `JSON.parse` karo.
Service worker ko `/static/js/sw.js` par rakh kar poori site offline hone ki ummeed karna. Default scope script ki directory hai.
revision: HTML validation = UX; server validation = security.
Web Storage sirf strings, per-origin; server ko nahi jaata (cookies jaati hain).
Custom element naam mein hyphen zaroori: `user-card`.
PWA = manifest + service worker + HTTPS; SW scope = script ki directory.
Native semantic elements pehle, ARIA baad mein; contrast ≥ 4.5:1.
SEO: unique title, h1, crawlable links, server-rendered content.

questions.question: In mein se kaunsa naam `customElements.define(naam, SomeClass)` se valid custom element ke roop mein register ho sakta hai?
questions.explanation: Custom element ke naam mein kam se kam ek hyphen hona chahiye aur woh lowercase letter se shuru ho, isliye `user-card` valid hai. Hyphen ka rule future ke built-in HTML tags (jinme hyphen nahi hota) se clash rokta hai. Option D ka trap: underscore ko hyphen jaisa separator samajhna. Option A mein hyphen nahi, aur option C mein hyphen to hai par naam digit se shuru hota hai.

questions.question: Signup form mein ab `<input type="email" name="email" required>` hai. Server-side validation ke baare mein sahi kya hai?
options: Server par phir bhi validate karna zaroori hai, kyunki browser validation devtools, curl ya script se bypass ho sakti hai
Ab server validation ki zaroorat nahi, browser invalid email bhejega hi nahi
`required` attribute server par bhi apne aap check hota hai
`type="email"` yeh bhi verify kar deta hai ki email address sach mein maujood hai
questions.explanation: HTML validation sirf browser mein, user ki convenience ke liye chalti hai; koi bhi seedha HTTP request bana kar khaali ya galat field bhej sakta hai. Option B ka trap: normal user ka experience dekh kar maan lena ki har request browser se hi aayegi. Option C galat hai kyunki server ko HTML attributes dikhte hi nahi, aur option D sirf format check karta hai, mailbox ka hona nahi.

questions.question: Browser console mein yeh code chalaya gaya. Output kya hoga?
questions.explanation: Web Storage sirf strings rakhta hai, isliye number 5 string '5' ban kar store hota hai aur `getItem` '5' lautata hai. String + 1 concatenation hai: '51', aur `typeof v` 'string'. Option A ka trap: maan lena ki storage type yaad rakhta hai. Option B output sahi padhta hai par type galat, aur option C maanta hai ki string aur number jodne se NaN aata hai; JS mein `+` string milte hi concatenation karta hai, NaN nahi deta.

questions.question: In mein se kaunsa client-side storage browser **har matching HTTP request ke saath apne aap** server ko bhejta hai?
options: Cookies (jo us domain aur path se match karein)
questions.explanation: Cookies browser khud har matching request ke `Cookie` header mein lagata hai; isi wajah se sessions kaam karte hain aur isi wajah se CSRF bhi possible hota hai. Option A ka trap: localStorage bhi 'login data rakhne ki jagah' ke roop mein mashhoor hai, par woh tab hi server tak jaata hai jab JavaScript use khud request mein daale. Options B aur D bhi sirf browser ke andar rehte hain.

questions.question:
Ek page par Save button aise bana hai: `
Save
`. Mouse se click theek kaam karta hai. Sabse badi problem kya hai?
options: Keyboard se ispar focus nahi hota aur Enter/Space se activate nahi hota, aur screen reader ise button nahi batata; native `<button type="button">` use karna chahiye
Koi problem nahi, kyunki mouse click kaam kar raha hai
Sirf styling ki problem hai; CSS se button jaisa dikha do to sab theek
`div` SEO ke liye kharab hai, isliye page rank girega
questions.explanation: Native `<button>` mein focus, Enter/Space se activation aur 'button' role muft milte hain; `div` mein yeh sab nahi, isliye keyboard aur screen reader users Save nahi kar paate. Option C ka trap: accessibility ko sirf look ka masla samajhna; CSS role ya keyboard behaviour nahi deta. Option B sirf mouse users ko dekhta hai, aur option D asli problem (accessibility) ko chhod kar galat cheez pakadta hai.

questions.question: Ek HTTPS site `/dashboard` page se `navigator.serviceWorker.register('/static/js/sw.js')` call karti hai (koi `scope` option nahi, koi `Service-Worker-Allowed` header nahi). Yeh service worker kin pages ko control karega?
options: Poori site, yaani `/` se shuru hone wale saare pages
Sirf `/dashboard`, kyunki usi page ne register kiya
Koi page nahi, kyunki service workers localhost aur HTTPS dono par mana hain
Sirf `/static/js/` ke andar ke URLs; `/dashboard` control nahi hoga. Poori site ke liye `sw.js` ko `/sw.js` par serve karo
questions.explanation: Service worker ka default scope uski script ki directory hai: `/static/js/sw.js` ka scope `/static/js/` hai, aur header ke bina woh isse upar (jaise `/`) scope le bhi nahi sakta. Isliye `/dashboard` uske control mein nahi aata. Option A ka trap: maan lena ki register karne wali site ka har page apne aap control hota hai. Option B scope ko registering page se jodta hai, jo galat hai, aur option C ulta hai: service workers ko secure context chahiye, jisme HTTPS aur localhost dono aate hain.

questions.question: `sessionStorage` mein rakha data kab tak rehta hai?
options: Hamesha ke liye, browser band karne ke baad bhi
Har HTTP request ke saath server ko jaata hai, aur server use mitata hai
Sirf us tab ke khule rehne tak
questions.explanation: `sessionStorage` us tab tak seemit hai: tab band hua to data gaya. Option A ka trap: yeh `localStorage` ka behaviour hai, jo browser band karne ke baad bhi rehta hai. Option B cookies jaisa hai; storage APIs server ko apne aap nahi jaate. Option D jaisi koi fixed expiry nahi hoti.

questions.question: PWA mein **Web App Manifest** file ka kaam kya hai?
options: Install ke liye app ka naam, icons, `start_url` aur `display` batana
Network requests pakad kar Cache API se offline responses dena
Server se users ko push notifications bhejna aur schedule karna
Site ka HTTPS certificate aur private key surakshit rakhna
questions.explanation: Manifest ek JSON file hai jo browser ko batati hai ki app install hone par kaisi dikhe aur kahan se khule. Option B ka trap: offline responses service worker ka kaam hai, manifest ka nahi. Option C notifications ka alag API hai, aur option D server/TLS ki baat hai.

questions.question: WCAG AA ke hisaab se normal size ke text aur uske background ke beech kam se kam kitna contrast ratio chahiye?
questions.explanation: Normal text ke liye AA level ka minimum 4.5:1 hai. Option A ka trap: 3:1 bade text (large text) ke liye allowed hai, normal ke liye nahi. Option C (7:1) zyada sakht AAA level hai, aur option B kisi level ke liye kaafi nahi.

questions.question: Browser console mein yeh code chalaya gaya. Dono lines mein kya print hoga?
questions.explanation: `localStorage` sirf strings rakhta hai; object seedha do to woh `String(obj)` yaani `[object Object]` ban jaata hai aur data kho jaata hai. Doosre case mein `JSON.stringify` se `{"id":3}` store hua, `JSON.parse` ne wapas object diya, aur `id` number 3 hai, to 3 + 1 = 4. Option C ka trap: sochna ki object apne aap JSON ban jaayega. Option D maanta hai ki parse ke baad bhi value string hai (`'3' + 1`), aur option A dono galtiyan saath karta hai.

questions.question: Ek site ka menu aise bana hai: `Pricing`. Users ke liye click theek chalta hai. SEO ke liye sabse badi problem kya hai?
options: Span ka colour aur underline link jaisa nahi dikhta
`onclick` handler page ko kaafi slow kar deta hai
Pricing page ka `<title>` aur meta description galat hain
Crawlers sirf `<a href>` links follow karte hain, span wala nahi
questions.explanation: Search engine crawlers `<a href>` se pages dhoondte hain; JS click handler wala span unke liye link hai hi nahi, to pricing page shayad discover hi na ho. Saath hi keyboard aur screen reader users bhi ise link nahi samajhte. Option A styling ki baat hai, option B performance ka myth hai, aur option C ke baare mein yahan koi jaankari nahi; problem markup mein hai.

questions.question: Service worker `/app/sw.js` par hai aur `/app/start` page se `navigator.serviceWorker.register('/app/sw.js')` (koi `scope` option nahi) call hota hai. In pages mein se kaunse yeh worker control karega: `/app/`, `/app/reports/q3`, `/apps`, `/help`?
options: Charon pages, kyunki site ek hi origin hai
questions.explanation: Default scope script ki directory hai: `/app/`. Worker un URLs ko control karta hai jo `/app/` se shuru hote hain: `/app/` aur `/app/reports/q3` (subfolders bhi). `/apps` sirf "app" letters se shuru hota hai, `/app/` (slash ke saath) se nahi, isliye bahar hai; `/help` bhi bahar. Option C ka trap: prefix ko slash ke bina padhna. Option B scope ko register karne wale page se jodta hai, aur option D origin ko scope samajhta hai.

questions.question: In naamon ko `customElements.define(naam, SomeClass)` se register karne ki koshish ki gayi: `user-card`, `UserCard`, `my-Button`, `x-1`, `card`. Kaunse naam valid hain?
questions.explanation: Custom element naam lowercase letter se shuru ho, usme hyphen ho, aur koi uppercase letter na ho. `user-card` aur `x-1` teeno shartein poori karte hain. `UserCard` mein na hyphen hai aur uppercase bhi hai, `my-Button` mein uppercase B hai, aur `card` mein hyphen nahi. Option A ka trap: sochna ki hyphen ke baad digit allowed nahi. Option B uppercase ko ignore karta hai, aur option D hyphen ki shart bhool jaata hai.

questions.question: Yeh script page load par chalti hai. Fresh browser mein page teen baar load (reload) kiya gaya. **Teesre** load par console mein kya aayega?
questions.explanation: Load 1: `n` null, `Number(null)` = 0, `next` = 1, store `'1'`, log `1 11` (`getItem` string deta hai, `'1' + 1` = `'11'`). Load 2: `n` = `'1'` → next 2, store `'2'`. Load 3: next 3, store `'3'`, log `3 31`. Option A ka trap: `getItem` ki value ko number samajhna. Option C `Number()` ke bina string jodte rehne ka result hai, aur option D maanta hai ki `localStorage` reload par khaali ho jaata hai (aisa nahi hota; reload par `sessionStorage` bhi bacha rehta hai).

questions.question: Service worker active hai aur user offline ho gaya. Woh teen requests karta hai: `/static/app.css`, `/courses` aur `/`. Kya hoga?
options: Teeno fail, kyunki offline hone par service worker nahi chalta
Teeno chalenge, kyunki service worker sab kuch apne aap cache kar leta hai
Sirf `/` chalega, kyunki cache sirf HTML ke liye hai
`/static/app.css` aur `/` cache se milenge; `/courses` ka fetch fail hoga
questions.explanation: Cache-first: pehle `caches.match`. CSS aur `/` cache mein hain, to network ki zaroorat hi nahi, offline bhi mil jaate hain. `/courses` cache mein nahi, to `fetch` chalta hai, jo offline hone par reject hota hai: request fail. Option A ka trap: service worker ko network ka hissa maanna; woh browser ke andar chalta hai, isliye offline mein hi kaam aata hai. Option B: yeh code sirf padhta hai, cache mein kuch daalta nahi. Option C: Cache API kisi bhi response ko rakh sakti hai.

weeks.title: Deployment, Configuration and Monitoring
weeks.summary: Is week aap environments aur config ko code se alag rakhna, production mein WSGI server aur workers, reverse proxy ka kaam, containers ka idea, migrations ke saath safe releases, aur logging aur monitoring (percentiles) seekhoge.
concepts: **Environments**: development (aapka laptop), testing/CI, staging (production jaisa, real users ke bina) aur production. Code sab jagah wahi hona chahiye, sirf configuration badle; environments jitne milte-julte (parity) honge, 'mere machine par to chal raha tha' wale bugs utne kam.

**Configuration aur secrets**: database URL, `SECRET_KEY`, API keys jaise values code mein hard-code mat karo; unhe **environment variables** se padho (`os.environ.get('DATABASE_URL', default)`). Secrets kabhi git mein commit mat karo; local `.env` file `.gitignore` mein rakho. Production mein debug hamesha off: debug mode error par interactive debugger kholta hai, jisse server par arbitrary code chal sakta hai.

**Production WSGI server**: `flask run` wala development server testing ke liye hai, production load aur security ke liye nahi. Gunicorn jaisa server kai worker processes chalata hai: `gunicorn -w 4 -b 0.0.0.0:8000 wsgi:app`. Sync workers ke liye common starting point (2 × CPU cores) + 1 hai; har sync worker ek waqt mein ek request sambhalta hai, to max throughput ≈ workers ÷ average request time.

**Reverse proxy**: Nginx jaisa server app ke aage baithta hai: HTTPS (TLS) terminate karta hai, `/static/` files seedha disk se deta hai, compression aur slow clients ki buffering karta hai, rate limiting aur kai app instances mein load balancing karta hai. Python code (views, templates) Gunicorn workers mein chalta hai. Proxy ke peeche app ko asli client IP aur scheme `X-Forwarded-For`/`X-Forwarded-Proto` headers se pata chalte hain.

**Containers**: **image** app, uski dependencies aur runtime ka read-only package hai; **container** us image ka chalta hua instance. Dockerfile image banane ki recipe hai, aur ek hi image dev, staging aur prod mein chalti hai; farak sirf environment variables ka. Containers ko stateless rakho: uploads aur database volumes ya managed services mein, kyunki container kabhi bhi replace ho sakta hai.

**Releases aur migrations**: schema changes Alembic/Flask-Migrate jaisi **migrations** se versioned aur repeatable hote hain, aur deploy ke dauraan chalte hain. Backups lo, health check endpoint (`/health`) rakho, aur rolling deploy (ek-ek instance badalna) se downtime bachao. Kuch toote to pichhle version par rollback ka raasta pehle se tay ho.

**Logging**: levels DEBUG < INFO < WARNING < ERROR < CRITICAL. Logger ka level threshold hai: usse neeche ke messages drop hote hain. Containers mein logs stdout par likho taaki platform unhe collect kare. Har log line mein request id jaisa context do, aur passwords, tokens ya personal data kabhi log mat karo.

**Monitoring**: request rate, error rate (5xx %), latency aur saturation (CPU, memory, DB connections) track karo, aur thresholds par alerts lagao. Latency ke liye **percentiles** (p50, p95, p99) dekho, average nahi: kuch bahut slow requests average ko bigaad dete hain aur 'typical' user ka experience chhupa dete hain. Nearest-rank method mein p-th percentile = sorted list mein rank ⌈p/100 × n⌉ wali value.

example.problem: Ek Flask app ko container mein pack karo jahan Gunicorn port 8000 par chale, aur config environment se aaye. Container ko 1 CPU mila hai. Kitne workers rakhoge, aur code badalne par image rebuild mein kya fast hota hai?
example.code:
FROM python:3.12-slim
WORKDIR /app
COPY requirements.txt .
RUN pip install --no-cache-dir -r requirements.txt
COPY . .
ENV PYTHONUNBUFFERED=1
EXPOSE 8000
CMD ["gunicorn", "--workers", "3", "--bind", "0.0.0.0:8000", "wsgi:app"]

# run (values are examples)
# docker build -t notes-app .
# docker run -e DATABASE_URL=postgresql://... -e SECRET_KEY=... -p 8000:8000 notes-app
steps: Workers: (2 × 1 CPU) + 1 = 3, isliye `--workers 3`. Yeh starting point hai; load test karke adjust karo.
`requirements.txt` pehle copy hota hai aur dependencies alag layer mein install hoti hain. Sirf app code badle to yeh layer cache se reuse hoti hai, sirf `COPY . .` ke baad ka hissa dobara banta hai.
`DATABASE_URL` aur `SECRET_KEY` image mein nahi, `docker run -e` se aate hain; wahi image staging aur production dono mein chalti hai.
`PYTHONUNBUFFERED=1` se logs turant stdout par aate hain, jahan se platform unhe collect karta hai.
Production mein iske aage Nginx (ya cloud load balancer) HTTPS terminate karke requests container ke port 8000 par bhejta hai.
Answer: **3 workers**, aur code change par **dependency layer cache se reuse** hoti hai.

mistakes: `app.run(debug=True)` ke saath production chalana. Development server production ke liye nahi bana, aur debugger kisi ko bhi server par code chalane ka mauka de sakta hai.
`SECRET_KEY` ya database password ko code mein likh kar git par push karna. History se secret hatana mushkil hai; key rotate karo aur env vars use karo.
Sirf average latency monitor karna. Average 'theek' dikh sakta hai jabki har 10 mein se 1 user ko 2 second lag rahe hon; p95/p99 dekho.
revision: Same code, alag config: env vars se, secrets git se bahar.
Production: debug off, Gunicorn jaisa WSGI server, workers ≈ (2 × cores) + 1.
Nginx: TLS, static files, buffering, load balancing; Python Gunicorn mein.
Image = package, container = running instance; containers stateless.
Logger level se neeche ke messages drop; logs stdout par.
Latency ke liye percentiles; nearest-rank = ⌈p/100 × n⌉.

questions.question: Production server par Flask app ko `debug=True` ke saath chalana khatarnaak kyun hai?
options: Kyunki isse app thodi slow ho jaati hai, bas itni si baat hai
Kyunki error par interactive debugger aur poore tracebacks khulte hain, jisse code aur config leak hote hain aur debugger se server par arbitrary Python chalaya ja sakta hai
Kyunki debug mode mein templates load nahi hote
Kyunki debug mode HTTPS ko band kar deta hai
questions.explanation: Debug mode ka debugger browser mein Python console deta hai; production mein yeh remote code execution ka raasta hai, aur tracebacks secrets aur code structure dikhate hain. Option A ka trap: debug ko sirf performance ka masla samajhna, jabki asli khatra security ka hai. Options C aur D debug mode ke behaviour se mel nahi khaate; templates aur HTTPS (jo proxy sambhalta hai) dono par iska aisa asar nahi.

questions.question: Is shell mein na `DATABASE_URL` set hai na `FLASK_DEBUG`. Code ka output kya hoga?
questions.code:
import os

db_url = os.environ.get('DATABASE_URL', 'sqlite:///dev.db')
debug = os.environ.get('FLASK_DEBUG', '0') == '1'
print(db_url, debug)
questions.explanation: `os.environ.get(key, default)` key na milne par default lautata hai, to `db_url` dev SQLite URL hai. `FLASK_DEBUG` bhi missing hai, to `'0' == '1'` False. Option C ka trap: `get` ko `os.environ['DATABASE_URL']` jaisa samajhna, jo missing key par KeyError deta. Option B default ko ignore karta hai, aur option D comparison ke bajaye raw default '0' print karta hai.

questions.question: Server mein 4 CPU cores hain aur Gunicorn sync workers ki sankhya (2 × cores) + 1 rakhi gayi. Har request average 200 ms tak worker ko busy rakhti hai (zyadatar DB ka wait). Har sync worker ek waqt mein ek request sambhalta hai. Lagbhag maximum throughput kitna hoga?
questions.explanation: Workers = 2 × 4 + 1 = 9. Ek worker 200 ms mein ek request, yaani 1 ÷ 0.2 = 5 requests/s. Kul ≈ 9 × 5 = 45 requests/s. Option B ka trap: workers ki jagah cores (4 × 5) se multiply karna; sync worker DB ka wait karte waqt bhi busy rehta hai, aur yahan workers 9 hain. Option A sirf workers ginta hai, aur option D ek worker ka throughput hai.

questions.question: Is code ka output kya hoga?
questions.code:
import logging

logging.basicConfig(level=logging.WARNING, format='%(levelname)s:%(message)s')
log = logging.getLogger('shop')
log.debug('cart loaded')
log.info('order placed')
log.warning('stock low')
log.error('payment failed')
options: Chaaron messages, har ek apne level ke saath
questions.explanation: Threshold WARNING hai: is level aur usse upar (ERROR, CRITICAL) ke messages print hote hain, DEBUG aur INFO drop ho jaate hain. `shop` logger ka apna level set nahi, to woh root ka WARNING level use karta hai. Option B ka trap: level ko 'sirf yahi level' samajhna, jabki yeh minimum hai. Option A level ko ignore karta hai, aur option C maanta hai ki sirf errors hi log hote hain.

questions.question: Production setup: Internet → Nginx → Gunicorn (Flask app). In mein se kaunsa kaam aam taur par **Nginx ka nahi** hota?
options: `/static/` ki CSS/JS files seedha disk se serve karna
Flask ke view functions chalana aur Jinja templates render karna
Requests ko kai Gunicorn instances mein load-balance karna
questions.explanation: Nginx Python code nahi chalata; views aur templates Gunicorn ke worker processes mein Flask chalata hai, aur Nginx requests unhe proxy karta hai. Option B ka trap: lagta hai ki static files bhi 'app ka hissa' hain, par unhe Nginx se dena hi best practice hai (fast, Python workers free). Options A aur D reverse proxy ke classic kaam hain.

questions.question: Ek endpoint ki 10 requests ki latencies (ms) hain: 80, 85, 90, 95, 100, 105, 110, 120, 130, 2000. Nearest-rank method (p-th percentile = sorted list mein rank ⌈p/100 × n⌉ wali value) se mean aur p90 kya hain?
questions.explanation: Sum = 2915, to mean = 2915 ÷ 10 = 291.5 ms; ek 2000 ms wali request ne average ko baaki 9 requests ke average (lagbhag 102 ms) se karib teen guna kar diya. p90: rank ⌈0.9 × 10⌉ = 9, aur 9th value 130 ms hai. Option C ka trap: p90 ko 'sabse bada' (yahan p100/max) samajhna. Option B mean ki jagah median (102.5) leta hai, aur option D rank 8 wali value padhta hai. Isi wajah se dashboards percentiles dikhate hain: 90% requests 130 ms ya kam mein poori hui.

questions.question: Docker mein **image** aur **container** ka sahi farak kya hai?
options: Image read-only package hai; container uska chalta hua instance
Container read-only package hai; image uska chalta hua instance
Dono ek hi cheez ke do naam hain, koi farak nahi
Container Dockerfile ka doosra naam hai; image uska build log
questions.explanation: Dockerfile recipe hai, image us recipe se bana read-only package, aur container us image ka running instance; ek image se kai containers chal sakte hain. Option B ka trap: dono ko ulta yaad rakhna. Option C farak hi mita deta hai, aur option D Dockerfile ko container samajh leta hai.

questions.question: Flask app ka `SECRET_KEY` kahan se aana chahiye?
options: `app.py` ke top par seedha string likh kar
Git mein commit ki gayi `config.py` file se
HTML template ke andar ek hidden input field se
questions.explanation: Secrets code mein nahi, environment variables se padhe jaate hain (`os.environ`), aur local `.env` file git se bahar rakhi jaati hai. Option A aur B ka trap: code ya committed file mein secret git history mein hamesha ke liye reh jaata hai. Option D use har user ke browser tak bhej deta hai.

questions.question: Team ke paas development, staging aur production environments hain. **Staging** ka main maksad kya hai?
options: Developer ke laptop par naya code likhna aur debug karna
Production jaisa setup, jahan bina real users ke release check ho
Sirf CI mein unit tests chalane ki ek alag jagah
Production database ka roz ka backup rakhne ki jagah
questions.explanation: Staging production jaisa (same config ka dhaancha, same image) hota hai par real users ke bina, taaki release ko asli jaisi halat mein check kar sako. Option A development ka kaam hai, option C CI/testing ka. Option D ka trap: backups alag cheez hain; staging ek chalta hua environment hai.

questions.question: Ek endpoint ko 120 req/s sambhalne hain. Har request ek sync worker ko average 250 ms busy rakhti hai, aur har sync worker ek waqt mein ek request sambhalta hai. Kam se kam kitne workers chahiye?
questions.explanation: Ek worker 1 ÷ 0.25 = 4 req/s sambhalta hai. 120 req/s ke liye 120 ÷ 4 = 30 workers (yaani 120 × 0.25). Option A ka trap: yeh ek worker ki capacity hai, workers ki ginti nahi. Option B ka trap: 0.25 se multiply karne ki jagah divide kar dena (120 ÷ 0.25). Option C har request ke liye ek worker maan leta hai, request time ignore karke.

questions.question: App Nginx reverse proxy ke peeche hai, aur logs mein har request ka client IP `127.0.0.1` aa raha hai. App ko user ka asli IP kaise pata chalega?
options: Yeh Nginx ka bug hai; proxy hata do
Proxy ke set kiye `X-Forwarded-For` header se
Request ke `Host` header se, jo browser bhejta hai
Request ke `User-Agent` header se, jo browser bhejta hai
questions.explanation: App ka TCP connection Nginx se aata hai, isliye app ko proxy ka IP dikhta hai. Nginx asli client IP `X-Forwarded-For` header mein aage bhejta hai (aur scheme `X-Forwarded-Proto` mein). Option A ka trap: yeh expected behaviour hai, bug nahi, aur proxy TLS, static files aur buffering ke liye zaroori hai. Option C site ka naam batata hai, aur option D browser ka.

questions.question: Ek endpoint ki 20 requests ki latencies (ms): 22, 15, 400, 18, 21, 12, 30, 19, 90, 25, 16, 14, 48, 22, 20, 35, 18, 27, 15, 24. Nearest-rank method (p-th percentile = sorted list mein rank ⌈p/100 × n⌉ wali value) se p50 aur p95 kya hain?
questions.explanation: Sorted: 12, 14, 15, 15, 16, 18, 18, 19, 20, 21, 22, 22, 24, 25, 27, 30, 35, 48, 90, 400. p50: rank ⌈0.5 × 20⌉ = 10 → 21 ms. p95: rank ⌈0.95 × 20⌉ = 19 → 90 ms. Option A ka trap: p95 ko sabse badi value (rank 20, yaani max) maan lena. Option B ek rank peeche padhta hai (9 aur 18). Option D median ka "do beech wali values ka average" wala tareeka (21 + 22) ÷ 2 lagata hai, jo nearest-rank nahi hai.

questions.question: Is code se kaunsi log lines nikalengi?
questions.code:
import logging

logging.basicConfig(level=logging.INFO, format='%(levelname)s %(name)s %(message)s')
app = logging.getLogger('app')
db = logging.getLogger('app.db')
db.setLevel(logging.ERROR)

app.info('start')
db.warning('slow query')
db.error('timeout')
app.debug('cache miss')
options: 2 lines: `INFO app start` aur `ERROR app.db timeout`
3 lines: `INFO app start`, `WARNING app.db slow query`, `ERROR app.db timeout`
4 lines, kyunki `basicConfig` sab kuch print karta hai
questions.explanation: `app` logger ka apna level nahi, to root ka INFO lagta hai: `info('start')` aata hai, `debug('cache miss')` (DEBUG < INFO) drop. `app.db` ka level ERROR set hai: `warning` drop, `error('timeout')` aata hai. Total 2 lines. Option B ka trap: `db` ke apne ERROR level ko ignore karke root ka INFO lagana. Option C maanta hai ki ERROR level poore `app` tree par lag gaya, aur option D level threshold ko hi bhool jaata hai.

questions.question: Config environment variables se load hoti hai. Output kya hoga?
questions.explanation: `APP_DB` set hai, to DB environment wali value se badal jaati hai. `APP_DEBUG` ki value string `'False'` hai; `.lower()` se `'false'`, jo `('1', 'true')` mein nahi, to `DEBUG` boolean False. Option B ka trap: sochna ki koi bhi non-empty string (`'False'` bhi) True ban jaayegi; yahan code explicit comparison karta hai. Option A maanta hai ki string seedha store hogi, aur option C environment override ko ignore karta hai.

questions.question: Load balancer ke peeche 4 container instances hain. Har instance ko 1 CPU mila hai aur Gunicorn sync workers (2 × cores) + 1 hain; har request worker ko average 60 ms busy rakhti hai. Peak traffic 160 req/s hai. Rolling deploy (ek baar mein ek instance bahar) ke dauraan capacity kitni hogi, aur kya traffic sambhal paayega?
options: 150 req/s; nahi, isliye deploy se pehle ek extra instance jodo ya kam traffic ka time chuno
100 req/s; nahi, kyunki deploy mein aadhe instances bahar hote hain
150 req/s; haan, kyunki load balancer extra requests ko hamesha queue kar leta hai
questions.explanation: Workers = 2 × 1 + 1 = 3 per instance. Ek instance = 3 ÷ 0.06 = 50 req/s, to 4 instances = 200 req/s. Rolling deploy mein ek instance bahar: 3 × 50 = 150 req/s, jo 160 se kam hai, to overload. Option A ka trap: deploy ke dauraan bhi poori capacity maan lena. Option C rolling deploy ko "aadhe instances bahar" samajhta hai, aur option D queue ko capacity maan leta hai; queue sirf latency badhata hai, throughput nahi.
